I haven't put many hours into this game as I write this review, but here goes anyway.  I would recommend this game for people who like the genre.  This genre isn't for everyone, but if they're interested enough to be reading the reviews I figure they're going to like playing this one.  I know this game has officially launched and there is enough content to justify it as a finished game, but I still feel there is more room for expansion in the premise and execution of the game.
Likes:
Humor - I love the humor brought to this game.  It is deeper and more prevalent than the humor used in previous games of the type.  (I'm still a bit uneasy referring to this as a genre, but more on that later.)  I seldom finish the campaign modes in the other games like this, but the humor is actually enticing enough to make me want to see what they are going to say next in each successive mission.  I might actually finish the campaign in this one.
Graphic Art - Very well done.  I see a lot of good things in this game.  DK2 was breakthrough for its time as a novel concept, but the art was admittedly lackluster.  They made up for it with some rather nice video cutscenes after each level, but you don't spend hours staring at the cut scenes so having a pleasant viewing experience is definitely a plus.
Characterization - Something new to the genre and I like it.  Pretty much the only character you had to relate to in previous games was the narrator.  (Not that this was a bad thing, as there have been some pretty cool narrators for this type of game so far.)
Dislikes:
Better physics - The ragdoll effect for the heroes getting tossed about is nice, but the legs tend to go everywhere and while I might look like a sadist in saying this, as I was watching the heroes get tortured I couldn't help but notice the limbs would stick out at funny angles and it kind of ruined the effect.  This needed a bit more polish.
Is it really a genre? - I've only seen a few games like the old DK series which for me sort of got it all started.  For me though for it to classify as a genre you have to 1) hold to a common central theme and mechanics, and 2) you have to show enough original material to set yourself apart from others in what you are calling a genre or else you come off as nothing but a bunch of carbon copy clones of each other with now originality.  This game does well with the first point keeping a lot of the same mechanics from the other games in the genre, but it lacks anything very original.  It comes off as a carbon copy of other games of it's type (albeit with improved humor, characterization, graphics, etc.).  I had my hopes up high when I saw that the levels were randomly generated.  Having seen this now it isn't much to crow about yet.
So for me, Three Likes minus Two Dislikes still equals Recommend.
Stuff I would like to see in either DLC or further titles in the series:
Overworld buildings - Not many, but if you had something like an Orc Camp you could build next to your overworld assets where you could place things like the war drum or a watch tower it would make for some interesting strategies.  Other intersting ideas: dungeon entrances (a similar concept to the demonic portal, only persistent with the downside being heroes can invade through it.
More enslavement spells or rooms.  The randomly generated rooms with worms, dragons, and spiders, are nice.  Having a creature species or room that allows taming of these beasts would be awesome.  Process flow would be - Discover mother dragon, build creature pen, defeat dragon, snots drag to pen, drop in the taming room, horde member tames dragon, New creature to play with.
Terrain - One thing I see lacking in this game that I have seen in others is the use of terrain.  The dungeon zone in this game seems somewhat limited.  Other games offer underground lakes, lava pits, chasms, and the like.  I find the dungeon zones here somewhat basic.  I would like to see a map where you need to hop back and forth from overworld to dungeon to reach your goal.  There doesn't really seem to be a correlation between above ground and dungeon maps except at the entrance.
Creature dependent rooms - Not only do I think having certain creatures working specific rooms to be nice, I think that having a certain creature in your arsenal before you can build certain rooms/machines works too.  Especially when teamed with building overworld buildings.  As with the mechanics above for taming creatures something like - tame spider, train spider up to level four to promote to mother spider, send mother spider to overworld, sacrifice mother spider to create a spider nest which spawns (unconctrolled) baby spiders peridoically to harass nearby heroes.
Creature flavor:  I view the horde as basic units.  I tried skipping them to work with only units from other factions and it doesn't work very well.  I think "flavoring" horde units to a preferred faction would be fun.  This would also work if you install the ability to tame ambient creatures.  I could be as cosmetic as a different skin with a name/prefix change (undead orc/demonic orc, bone dragon/dark drake), or as a power boost to the unit.
All around, excited to see what the future holds for the game.

I'm not a big fan of "Free To Play" games, but after being hounded by a few friends to pick the game up, I gave it a shot.  I was a big fan of the original Tribes game, but I thought the series lost a lot of its luster with Tribes 2 and it completely fell off the wagon with the release of Tribes 3.
However, Hi Rez studios has found its magic once again with Tribes Ascend.  If you're a fan of First Person shooters, this is a must-play game for you.  It's not based on realism, so Call of Duty fans may be disappointed when it takes more than a single bullet to kill you, and Halo fans will find themselves a little more squishy than they're used to. However, I think after some adjustment, every gamer who likes the fast paced thrill of a good first person shooter will love this game.  By balancing maneuverability, firepower, and strategy, Tribes has taken your traditional First Person Shooter to a whole new dimension.  That dimension doesn't have a fancy name either, we call it simply the "third."  Jet packs man, we have them.
The game's entirely free to play and the game is fairly itemized and reasonably monetized.  Learn from my mistakes though, and only purchase something once for the VIP status.  Impatience is the only reason you'll ever spend more than $10.00 on this game.

It has a few base factions, each with their own design, but you can also create your own faction by picking an existing faction design. selecting an affinity, and picking perks to customise the game to your liking. Furthermore, the game is moddable, so with a bit of technical skill you can change the entire game around if you want.
If you can excuse a few bugs, Endless Space is definitely worth looking at if you enjoy space strategy.
Take a look at my screenshots for a few impressions.

I will preface my review by saying that Metroidvania/Bullet Hell is NOT my go-to genre and this is my first dive into either of them after a long, long time. I bought this game mostly on the preface that it is in the anime category and it was more action oriented. While I do play a lot of the dating sims on Steam, this kind of has the look and feel of a weird hybrid. The action is great and it's fun to learn to control the two very different characters. The artwork and deluxe edition are also worth the money and this is an indie title that is well deserving of the investment of time. I really like a lot of the characters and the dialogues and I love the world they live in and how fun it is to look at.
However, I do have a few negatives..but they do not really take away from the enjoyment of this game. The story is a bit silly, over-the-top and kind of weak, but I have yet to finish it. Do not go into Rabi-Ribi expecting a dead-out serious ride with lots of lore, it's supposed to be kind of fantasy/out there and I can see past that and a few character discrepancies.
I also do not feel like a lot of the game directs you on where to go if you are a beginner, I'm still kind of early on and sometimes I just do not know how to reach certain areas to progress. It's very much a sit-down and figure it out game, I found the tutorials kind of lacking in a few areas.
But I think the pro to this idea is that you will not run out of things to do before clocking a lot of hours in this charming game and it does take you back to the days when you really had to work at and master a title while completing it.

I have been playing this game well before it became part of the Gaben (Steam). The game feels like the classic Mechwarrior Games of old plus Each mech you own you can customize the paint job, the engine, the weapons, etc to fit your play style. They have both mechs of the Inner Sphere and the clans and been adding more. Gameplay is challenging for those who never played the original Mechwarrior games so the learning curb is a bit high, but there are units (guilds in the game) you could join and learn to off of. The community is mostly friendly as well so a new guy can learn well from veteran players. Mechs can be purchased by money (which is converted to MC) or the in game C-bills. The good thing is parts for your mech except for paint and camo can be bought only with C-bills which prevents the game going completely pay to win. (the hero/champion mechs that you can buy with MC only are just a different variant of the mechs with a C-bill bonus attached. Nothing more.) Camo and cosmetic items are MC only as well, but the game does have events that pop up that you can earn C-bills, items, and MCs
The only problems I have with the game is that Community Warfare needs a bit more balancing in order to make the battles fair for both Clan and IS forces. They also should keep with the event formula they did with last week's which you get rewards once you hit a total accumulated number of points instead of previous events going for the 'you need this many per match to qualify' I hated that way and love the accumulation number much more since I managed to get everything in last week's event.
Last, but not least they need to do better with the mech packs. 20 is fine for a mech pack, but over that is too much for me, AlThough you can wait until the mech you want is purchasable by C-bills.
That said if you a mech fan or someone who wants a bit of a challenge game I recommend MWO. If your not either of these there are plenty of other games on steam/GOG.

Mechwarrior Online came with great promises and expectations in 2012, hoping to revive the abandoned genre of Battletech, which was one of the most influential genres back in the 90's. There hasn't been a real Mechwarrior PC game since year 2000, so when the MW:O was announced, hype was real and genuine. The developers of Mechwarrior Online, PGI, stated that MW:O is going to be a credible representation of the rich Battletech universe, with tactical combat, simulator experience of piloting a battlemech, including a large, community driven territory expansion and character development ecosystem, combined with real-time lore timeline progression. PGI called their game “thinking man's shooter”, due to how deep the battlemech customization, information warfare and combat roles are compared to any other arena shooters in the market.
They weren't entirely wrong, but MWO left a lot of things to be desired. Game has been available for 3 years, however many of the promised features are not in the game, will never be implemented, or are bare bone functional.
MWO offers  two game modes, available to any player. First mode, called “Quick Play”, is an arena game team deathmatch mode, where a matchmaker puts you on a random map of 13, with random people within your skill pool. There is nothing particularly worth mentioning, it is a Team Deathmatch of 12 players per team with no respawns. A quick, straightforward game mode, with high ingame currency and experience gain ratio. It is a recommended game mode for new players, until they grasp the basics of the game, then maybe join a clan and select their faction.
Second game mode is called “Faction Play”, previously known as Community Warfare. This is an advanced game mode, meant for intermediate players. You can play it as a novice, but you will be severely handicapped by doing that. FP/CW is a team deathmatch with objectives, where a team has to defend or destroy a mission objectives on the map to win the match. It is a slightly deeper in regards to tactics and drop preparation, since you can take up to 4 battlemechs in a match, however it is more time consuming and less currency friendly than Quick Play. This is meant to be the main game mode, but is currently in BETA 2, which is a PGI term for not complete. It should receive a  significant updates in the future, but is severely lacking currently.
Mechwarrior Online is a game that is really unique in this genre. It is the only mech combat simulator on the market, and the feeling of piloting a giant combat machine is really outstanding. This is the thing PGI got right. Unfortunately not many other things are on the same level. Once you make through very basic new player experience, you will have a limited amount of really good experience exploring new maps, battlemechs and different strategies, but once the dust settles, MWO is only a mediocre team deathmatch arena shooter with mechs, played on a seriously flawed maps, lacking the promised combat roles and information warfare. Severely lackluster game modes, combined with slow content release cycle and non-evolving balance due negligence of developers leaves little hope for the future of the game.

I am a “Legendary Founder”; One of the original financial backers of the game from over three years ago. I have hundreds of hours logged in. I've been on TS3 with the devs during the closed beta, participated in guild matches, fought through solo matches, You name it. Hell, My name's even listed in the game's credits (Along with the other legendary Founders).I may not have time logged in with Steam, But I'm about as creditable a source as anyone out there for the condition of this game.

I typed up a massive, 70,000-ish character long review, -then- found out about the 8,000 character limit on Steam reviews. LOL.

Every aspect of this game is sub-par:
Shallow, dull, repetitive game play with zero sense of accomplishment or momentum. Since early beta, to today, and I'm sure into the future, You will never see anything other then team death matches in poorly built arenas, usually with the same few builds.
MWO is yet another game that touts a customization system with several different weapons and equipment... But throws you into the exact same scenarios over and over again, there by negating customization all together.
Why equip flamers if the terrain can't be set on fire? Why pack machine guns if You'll never encounter non-mech units? Why spec Yourself for scouting when You know damned well that the OpFor is going down lane A (as usual) and the fight's going to be at center (as usual)?
There's the “Skill Tree”... That's not actually a tree: It doesn't branch off anywhere. And it's the exact same set of skills for every mech. A 20 ton “scout” mech has access to the exact same skills as a 100 ton “assault” mech, and vice-versa.
Imagine if Borderlands gave all four characters the exact same skill tree, then, instead of having limited level points to spend, there by making You sacrifice access to some perks for others, it just let You collect XP infinitely, So You could have ALL of the skills. There would be almost no difference between the characters themselves, the play style of the players, OR the actions taken in-game.
No sacrifices, No limits, No differences, No point.
The devs pride Themselves on this being a “Minimally Viable Product”. As long as the software boots up, it's A-okay in PGI's books. Never mind the myriad of missing, incomplete, or poorly-deployed game mechanics that were promised to us three years ago. Or various bugs.
PGI have a proven record of flat-out lying about features, time frames, content, pretty much everything.
Their pricing models are a complete joke. Buying “Premium time” only get's You a paltry 50% bonus, on top of already meager cash and XP earnings. Purchasing “Hero” mechs only net You a 30% bonus. And the COST of said premium items are hideous; 15-to-60 USD for a Mech pach, which is little more that a skin change in this game. And said prices have never, and WILL NEVER go down. Sure, there are sales every now and then, but the base prices never budge. Even on the crumby, unpopular mechs.
Then there's PGI's habit of releasing a mech for cash with a bunch of really attractive features and quirks, then when the mech cycles down to free access, or when the next hero mech is ready for sale, They nerf the crud out of it, butchering the value of the mech and screwing over the purchaser in the process. And then They call it “A balance pass”.
And speaking of balance:
Hol. E. Crap.
Several of the original balancing systems (Repair and Rearm costs, Weapon convergence, logistics, operational costs,
availability, engagement rules, to name a few) were gutted early or never implemented to begin with, leaving a huge gaping hole where balance would be.
Without a means of limiting the more powerful or useful weapons, equipment, and mechs, PGI has, for the past three years been whipping out heavy-handed, non-nonsensical, arbitrary, un-intuitive, and just plain bizarre band-aid fixes.
And once something actually works reliably, the players themselves will complain about it “being OP' or “Unfair” until PGI guts that system too.
Graphics and audio even kind of blow here.
The LoD models are utter garbage, making every mech look like a gray blob at anything other then close range.
Several mechs have pointlessly low-res textures, making them look fuzzy, while other mechs are nice and crisp.
The environments are mostly static, save for a few trees You can knock down. Even if You unload every weapon You have into the side of a building, You don't even see a generic “black n' burnt” decal or smoke. Just nothing.
The environments are intentionally designed so that no matter what vision mode (normal, Thermal, night) You're in, You still can't see jack squat.
Sound is fine, but that's just it, only fine.
The arenas are horribly built. The hit boxes for terrain are often bigger then the textures, leading to a lot of shots being blocked by “Invisible” walls.
There's so much cover that it creates lanes, forcing matches into the same spots with the same tactics.
And since PGI just copied the vehicle code that comes with cryengine, all the mechs; 30 foot tall WALKING machines, can quite literally get hung up on rocks the size of said mech's toe. You can even stall out going up a somewhat steep hill, as again, the game treats giant WALKING machines as small cars.
And then there's the community:
When a game is online-only, the players are every bit a part of the game as code that drives it. And this community is just awful.
You've got the “Old Guards” that will insist that the custom house rules They play the tabletop game by are THE rules, claim to know it all, but have to consult Their rules books every five seconds like rookies.
There's the “Twitch-Tryhards”, that insist that every player treat the game like it was Their life, and  demand that You “git gud” join a guild, play the meta, or else.
There's the “YOLOSAWG420” types that are incapable of putting Their bongs down for five minutes, expect You to play as bad as Them, and are scared witless of actually TRYING to win, as that would mean risking failure, and failure would be, like, just totally uncool, brah.
The absolute worst though are the “White Knights”. These are a strange , rare, dwindling species of critter that are not only utterly devote to PGI, but will actively silence, harass, mock, belittle, and otherwise work to discredit any and all dissenting opinions, by any twist of logic available:
“This will help, but don't we have anything more potent? Don't we have a silver bullet that will just cause some of these thread to become so discredited that they will implode?”
-Discredit. Not debate, not refute, not challenge, not offer a different point of view. DISCREDIT
This is the caliber of people You'll be dealing with in-game. Either keep your eye's down, mouth shut, and take whatever foul-smelling brown substance They give You, or face the consequences.
In closing, go ahead and play the game. Hell, hammer Their servers with traffic, but never, EVER pay them anything. Even the minimum seven bucks MC package is too good for these hacks.

DOOM is a pretty freakin fantastic game. It's got a great story that can be easily ignored during second, third, or fourth playthroughs. The cutscenes (if you can call them that) last seconds at most and are far and few. However, in that short time, you can get this amazing world of demons and doomguys. The doomguy character in itself is amazing, the way he angrily reacts to Samuel Hayden's justification for the Argent Energy project (the one that caused this DOOM game, basically) tells an amazing story about your character, just by itself.
Aside from all the amazing story points this game has, it's actual playability is even better. There is nothing more cathartic than literally ripping in half a demon before doing a 360 and punching another one's head so hard it explodes. The difficulty levels are the first ones I've ever used in a game, because as time went on I actually got better at it. As of now, I've completed a nightmare run, a pistol-only run, every other difficulty run, and one kinda special run where you don't upgrade any weapons or your suit. They were all great.
Honestly I'm not sure why it says I have so few hours on DOOM. It feels like my most played game of 2017, and even though so far I don't have 2x the money cost in hours (which is my general rule for a good game), DOOM is definitely worth it.

Bought this product at my local GameStop in January of 2016.
Pros:
-Customizable beyond reason
-Usage outside of Steam (i.e. regular computer use)
-Tight response
-Pressure sensitive triggers (which can be bound as 2 different commands)
-Wireless
-GRIP BUTTONS
-BEEP BOOPS
-Community Downloadable controller layouts (This can be a blessing and a curse)
Cons
-Issues with loading the controller properly at times
-Non Rechargable batteries
-Not all games are properly optimized for this controller (but is managable with tweaking)
-Learning how to customize be confusing at first
**DISCLAIMER** This controller WILL take getting used to. At first I had a hard time adjusting to the touch pads, but after a few playthroughs of Borderlands 2, I have no issues with controlling the camera in normal FPS titles. One of my cons list "game optimization" as a factor, and that is quite true in a few ways. Camera control in Third Person games can be a pain to adjust where it doesn't feel like you're driving it with rubber bands. By that I mean it is quite difficult to coordinate in game camera sensitivity and controller sensitivity and takes some time before you can actually play the game. Platformers are just akward using the touch D-pad for control, and trying to push the touch pad in for every command is rough to accomplish. There is a way to change the scheme to play off of the touchpad, but it can be sloppy. I haven't really figured out how to properly play Super Meat Boy or Mega Man as effectively as I would with a standard D-Pad quite yet.
I feel like I need a week long class just to learn how to customize this controller properly to get what I want out of it.
I recommend buying this controller if you want something wireless and are willing to adapt to a new controller feel.

This controller is absolutely fantastic.  It's a polished hybrid between a classical controller concept and the added functionality of a mouse.  In the past I have absolutely abhored trackpads on laptops and such, but the pads on the Steam controller work extremely well and very sensitive and accurate.
To me, ultimately it comes down to the games and the genres.
2D Platformer like Super Meat Boy - Even better than the PS3 controller I was using before. The "d-pad" on this is accurate, responsive, and has great tactile feedback.
3rd Person Action like Dead Souls II - This is probably the number one use for this controller.  It feels incredibly responsive and after a few minutes of adaption the limitations of a mouse or analogue stick become apparent compared to the right track pad, for controlling the 3rd person camera.
Fighting Game like SF4 - Haven't actually tried this, since I dropped a bill on a Hori arcade style stick controller a few years back.  I should give it a try though, this controller has surprised me more than once.
Strategy/Sim - Not my cup of tea, so I couldn't say.
FPS like ... - This is where I think the controller is weakest.  Precise aiming with the track pad is a bit frusterating IMO, and it definitely cannot replace the precision and speed of a good mouse.
So yea, it's a really great controller, and I can't recommend it enough for those games that really beg for a controller in the first place.

Below is my original review that was very positive, below that is a revised version reflecting on Blockland since its release to Steam.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I've played this game for at least three years, four if you count the long time I spent on the Demo, and I've loved every minute of it.
It's like playing with Legos on the internet, only with user created content in quantities comparable to Garry's mod. You can quite literally do anything in this game, probably more so than any other sandbox game that claims that. And if you can't do it, then an add-on can probably be created to do it.
And it's also fantastic for making videos and stuff, here's some good YouTube channels that have a lot of BL videos.
I could add a lot more, but I don't want to start to spam. These are some of the more notable BL channels anyway.
------------------------------------------------------------------------EDIT------------------------------------------------
However,
I originally wrote this review when Blockland first came out on Steam, hoping along with the rest of the community for an influx of players that would revive the community and the game.
I was wrong.
It is true that the potential for this game is huge, and the possibilities are just about endless. But unfortunately it seems like that potential has been utterly wasted here. Lately I have played less and less of Blockland; the only things that bring me back to playing are the occasional friends who wants to play with me and the desire to keep my YouTube channel from dieing. Blockland as a game and a community is dieing.
I love the game, but it's nothing without creative, fun people to play and to create new things with. There are some people like that, but the majority of people who are attracted to this game are the contrary: too lazy and apathetic to put forth effort into creating, and too immature to have fun with.
If that were the only problem, I'd still wholly recommend this game, but it's not. The game's main forum only feeds this kind of behavior. It has an entire section devoted to allowing people to hash it out, point fingers, and create drama. The creator, while I respect him and am thankful for his game, only makes the issue worse. A lot of the time he directly feeds and instagates a lot of the drama on the forums and doesn't care enough to do anything about it. He bans from the forums for ludicrous reasons- sometimes purely because he feels like it.
Since getting rid of terrain and interiors- a major part of the game that gave players places to just screw around and have fun with each other, the only significant addition to the game was the S&S update in 2012. We were given shadows and shaders which, while they look great, require computers that most people who own the game don't have. Since then Blockland as a game and community has been neglected and has little to no future.
If there were updates that occasionally popped up; if the community wasn't constantly pushed into such a dead state; if there were still a few tutorials that taught people how to build, play, and create things so that maybe we would have a good server here and there rather than waiting against hope for a good one to show up on its own; if the creator gave a crap what his game turned into, this would be an awesome game that I would still recommend to all my friends. But the things in the trailer, while possible, won't happen. They are far and few inbetween, and if you ever want to make something like that on your own, it will take a lot of time and effort, not only to create it, but just to learn how. And if ever you do create something like that, people will frolic to it for a while and then everyone, including you, will get bored of it and forget it. You will have to start the process all over again, or else the game will remain as dead as when you got it.
For the price, sure, I'd say this game is worth $10. Buy it. But I don't recommend trying to get involved or in getting your hopes up. This game is going nowhere.

Ikarugua is a shooter hell game that was developedI by TREASURE, the same developer who made great classics like Gunstar Heroes, Guardian Heroes, Sin & Punishment, Radiant Silvergun, etc. This game was originally a Japan-exclusive game to the Arcades and the Dreamcast. It was released worldwide for the Nintendo Gamecube in 2003. This is game was also released to Xbox Live in 2011. then Steam port was released in February 18, 2014.
This game doesn't really feature power-ups, but it features a unique mechanic in exchange. This game allows you to change the prolarity of your ship to light and dark. If you chose the wrong polarity for the ship, you're basically screwed.
Ikarugua is really known for the challenge. Try playing it in hard mode, and you'll know why this game is seriously difficult. Ikarugua may be known for its difficulty, but it's also really addictive. The levels are really well-made and the music is really amazing in my opinion. The graphics are really good for this year. The Steam port of Ikarugua has gamepad support. I tested this game with a Xbox One controller, and it works pretty well. I'm not sure if this works with any gamepad other than a Xbox One controller, so can anyone please confirm it? The controls were very reponsive and stiff.
Just because this game is really good, that doesn't mean it has its flaws. One of the issues I have about this game is the story seems non-existent. The another issues is because of its difficulty, this game can possibly make someone throw a controller (or keyboard) to the wall. Ikaruga doesn't have many levels, and the levels are short if you mastered the game.
I recommend you to buy this game. It's one of the best shooters (Not counting FPS) in steam.

NARUTO SHIPPUDEN: Ultimate Ninja STORM 4 is the sequel to NARUTO SHIPPUDEN: Ultimate Ninja STORM 3. Before continuing the fight against Obito, you'll have to do some boss battles which are flashbacks. The story mode is pretty short if you don't skip the cutscenes (finishable in less than 3 hours). But if you haven't read the manga, I advice you not to skip them. They allow you to finish the anime (thanks fillers!) or to see the manga as animation. Or you can just watch them for fun! Counter to NSUNS3, NSUNS4 isn't open-world. But the adventure mode is here to satisfy you. For the rest of the game modes, it is standard: free battle mode (nothing changed), online mode (didn't try it out, yet), and Collection (where you can watch your ninja card, for example). The roster increased, some characters are available exclusively via pre-ordering the game, some others via downloadable content and the others, available in other games, didn't change.

Way too many loot drops - usually 4-5 items per encounter and you only have an inventory of 20 slots. So you spend too much time sorting through items. Also, combat is stat heavy yet somehow feels too simplistic since each character only has 2 skills, and from what I see there are no skill upgrades or ways to get new skills. And, the skills don't necessarily complement each other very well. To see a rogue-like done right, check out Darkest Dungeon. You have to really pay attention to balancing your team with that game, and each team member plays an important role. Here you can have all warriors, all wizards, all rogues etc. and be just fine as long as you have enough heal potions, which are very plentiful. So long story short, this is not a thinking person's game, it's just kill a group, get new loot, equip new loot, throw most of your lott away since your inventory is so limited, kill another group, make sure you have plenty of potions, rinse and repeat. Gets boring and very grindy FAST. On the plus side, some of the humor and random encounters are pretty funny. Like where you find a dog that leads you to a hole and starts digging, and then just pees in the hole and leaves. Lol!

If you want a game that you want to play everyday, but not for more than 30-35 mins a day - look no further. As of writing this, I have unlocked about 1/3rd of gun models in 53 hrs of game time, spread over 2.5 months. I would classify this game as basically a puzzle game with really accurate gun anatomy. The huge amount of available guns (100+ real life guns as of writing this) and the various modes of play are the huge plus points of this game. The shooting ranges, frankly, suck. The game does its basic job perfectly though, and that is reason enough for me to recommend it.
To all those crying about the paywall, I for a fact did NOT need to pay a single penny and still I haven't needed to "grind" any model. Once I get an achievement, I go for the next one. It is a little bit difficult in the beginning, especially the sniper and hardcore achievements, but once you are used to the game mechanics, in one or two half hour sessions, you can easily complete all achievements for a given model (Exceptions: The Top3 and Champion achievements are not doable for about the first 15-20 models you unlock; the more guns you unlock, the lesser people play those guns everyday and hence it gets slowly possible and later easier to score a Top Score of the day in at least one of the 3 modes.) Also, a very nifty way to score 20000 exp and 20 credits is to make sure 5 of your friends play WoG at least upto the tutorial disassembly. Save the credits to unlock 4 guns of requiring 5 credits each. Also, for each gun you score the daily top score, you get 1 credit. On top of that, you can do the quiz once every hour, and with a little practice/checking out the wiki for gun models, it is a piece of cake to score 1500-2400 exp every hour! Even if you do 2 quizzes of 30 seconds a day, it more than compensates for the difference between the total exp you earn from a gun and the exp you spent to unlock it. Stop ♥♥♥♥♥ing about it, it just shows how easily you give up.
For those who want something more than guns and dont mind paying, it also has the "Bonus" mode, where you can assemble and disassemble animal skeletons, classic cars and even the Captain America bike. Since each of the cars have close to a 1000 parts and the skeletons and bike more than 250 parts each, please think and make sure you're up to the task or you will just waste your money. Also, if at all you do spend money, DO NOT spend it on unlocking the gun map, or buying experience! My suggestion would be to spend on the bonus item packs for a greater challenge. I feel the gun map is more fun and challenging in its basic F2P setting. If you don't feel like going for champion achievement or your hands arent fast enough, you might consider buying a few credits to unlock some gun you want. Never waste money on exp, you can easily farm it from quizzes.
All in all, WoG is a great game, if you like to solve puzzles and memory games, or LOVE guns and machinery in general, or just want something casual to relax for 30 minutes a day. If you ticked "all of these" like me, you will also end up writing a nice review in a couple months! Just as a cherry on top, the developers are good and responsive, keep experimenting, updating, upgrading, bugfixing and releasing at least a couple models every month. And all this, for free. I don't know what else to say!

Very charming metroidvania style platformer. It has cute girls, and humorous dialogue. A+ soundtrack. The hard mode is unforgiving. The bosses incorporate danmaku (bullet hell) special attacks so it has a spin on your traditional platformer.
Non-linear which is nice, you get to chose how to progress through the game. It doesn't force you to go to any particular place. Really nice game, and worth the full price IMO.

This game was an amazing surprise and a game that makes me lament missing its crowdfunding.
For the short explanation of the game its a mix of platforming and Danmaku (Bullet Hell) shoot em ups, the nearest comparison I can give game play wise is a Touhou fan game series by the name of Koumajou Densetsu. The danmaku really comes out during boss fights which makes bosses very fun to fight each also coming with their own desperation moves which are similar to Touhou's "spell cards".
The platforming aspect of the game is also not lacking, while many of the games early enemies are throw away, there are still difficult non boss areas of the game that challenge a player's platforming skills. The game boasts a "metroidvania" style to its gameplay which allows a player outside of minor path forcing here and there to tackle the game in any order they wish. The level of thought they put into allowing the non linear approach was amazing, even allowing 0% item runs if you know the game and your skills well enough.
Lastly I want to discuss the cast and plot, which may come off weak in some areas. The overall plot itself without giving away spoilers... lets just say it kinda leaves some gaps in as to what happened, letting the player kinda decide for themselves which bugs me but its not all that horrible, its more of a minor personal gripe. Outside of the story the characters themselves are cute and quirky, many characters are parodies of famous anime and story characters from other series, but keep enough of their own charm to not be lame copies. I almost think of an old game from JAST called Season of Sakura for this, every single character was inspired from famous anime characters of the time yet they still were all their own characters at the same time.
In all this is a game that is deceptive, its a fun and amazingly challenging platformer hiding under a layer of cute. If cute doesn't bug you, give this game a shot. If you love cute, this game will be match made in heaven.
One last thing, part of what is making this game so great is the amazing amount of post release support the game is getting, even as I write this they are still adding content and fixing bugs. Simply amazing.
11/23/2016: many months later and everything I said still applies only even more magnified, the game is amazing and only a month ago they released an amazing free dlc for halloween thats seriously fun to play. I am not much of a company fan, but these guys are making it hard not to be, I am seriously impressed with their game and how they handle content.

[EDIT] Okay so actual review, after finishing the game after spending weeks on this game (I have a very short time on computer, and i really rarely play games) I must say, this is one if not, a large imrpovement compared to all games, and is the second best Neptunia game for me.
The story is really well-written, there are some plotholes and a bit of elements not explained, but this is Neptunia, where's the fun in it if everything is explained?
Its really good, pretty good, i went through all 3 endings, and all of it was worth it (P.S, bad end sucks really)
And other characters also get more fleshed out, at least, compared to RB3. Which is nice.
Now, story aside as i praised it like it's a masterpiece, next is the soundtrack, it's absolutely amazing, very well composed, and some of the soundtracks are made by well-known artists.
The techno-genre-ish / futuristic like soundtracks are great, although it may revolve around that, there are some other soundtracks that are peaceful, funny, upbeat and a bit sad.
The songs in this game are definitely good, i loved Mousou Karthasis (Spoilers!) of all songs in this game, although Zero Dimension's song was good as well.
Now, songs aside, performance is a bit... eh, there are some issues regarding potato specs computers, and well i recommend that you don't play this on a laptop unless you want it to burn.
It really requires a strong computer, since i played this game on a Quad Core Q6000 2.40GHz and a GT 730 4GB, i kinda stuttered in a lot of scenes, skills, cutscenes and whatnot.
It still good though, game still looks amazing even if the settings are lowered, so that's one good thing.
Overall gameplay is the same as other nep games, but of course, its updated, combos are now more useful as they have the effeciency system (Consistent combos) and there's more skills!
Updated skill animations, new EXE moves, and more that is added, definitely an improvement.
Replayability is...well, three times at best, assuming you want all endings, but overall I don't find Neptunia games to be super replayable, but moreso a one-time only story for me, Its still fun to read the tidbits of dialogues though and such.
Other than that, i don't have anything to say more, it's a pretty good JRPG game, and it's anime with the cutest protagonist ever made in existent, Neptune.
I'd say its a 9.5/10, to be honest, i'm biased to nep games, but even so, this is really good, a step higher up at least from the abomination called Re;birth 3.
So, without further ado, buy the game, download it, buy puddings, and play the game!

Dungeons 1 was weak, Dungeons 2 was somewhat better, Dungeons 3 nailed it.
It's a great game. Some say it is better than Dungeon Keeper 2 and improves upon it, but I would NOT go as far.
It is fun and entertaining, it is cool it breaks the 4th wall and is not all too serious - but I think they went way overboard with this, just... Too much. But that is personal opinion.
It does seem somewhat repetetive, as opposed to Dungeon Keeper games, where starting a new dungeon was always fun for some reason.
The coop is rather basic and there is no lobby system, the search for partner I think so far works only in Duel, and in other modes you compete in ammount of "evileness" and have to scout the live lobby chatter to punch room number by hand... Very strange and odd.
But that aside, the game works flawlessly.
~140 FPS on a 144hz monitor, despite literally no settings in options.
Game parodies Warcraft and LOTR a lot, which I think is very entertaining. Does not create any bond with characters, because it straight out tells you everything is a generic placeholder thing to kill (that's why I said they went overboard).
In such way they lessen the "evilness" of the overall game. Dark rooms of DK, screams from torture chambers and convincing voice acting is not there. It's just the narration to the mechanics you are going to repeat over and over again.
Thankfully the core of the game is very solid. The undeground part we know from DK and above it's simple RTS (without attack move command? argh...)
Still I would give it a solid 8/10. I've mostly focused on the criticism, just so nobody would feel cheated.

All right. I bought the Steam Controller with the Dark Souls 3 package.
7/10 (With potential for more)
For DS3, I find the controller
above average. I haven't delved fully into the customization options, but when I play DS3 I use it exclusively (because I only have a PS4 controller otherwise, and DS3 just can't recognize it). There are issues when I've encountered an enemy, and then I accidentally move my thumb across the touchpad and all of a sudden I'm looking down. Those of you familiar with the Dark Souls games know that this small setback can result in death for the unwary. I haven't yet died because of this happening, but it has happened several times.
I have found that another's configuration for the touchpad makes looking a lot easer, and have decided to go with their setup (I believe the person's name was "Haml4t."
I will say it DOES NOT seem to be preferred over kb/m for ALL GAMES. For DS3 I find I'd rather use it because of its playstyle, but the controller markets itself as a better option because you can also use it for first person shooters as effectively as kb/m. I briefly had DOOM (and then realized I couldn't run it well) and it was taxing, to say the least. Because of DOOM's playstyle (super fast-paced, twitch reaction time necessary) it seemed clunky. Using the right touchpad as the "mouse/joystick" combo is enough to make the controller usable, but you have to flick it to turn completely around, and the aiming feels a little imprecise. Using it as a mouse is way too sensitive. My framerate issue had nothing to do with the effectiveness of the Steam Controller in this situation.
Even a game like The Stanley Parable doesn't seem so smooth with the Steam Controller.  That one allows me to use either the SC or my PS4 controller, and I prefer the PS4 controller.
I will note that when you purchase DOOM, you're told you don't have full controller support, and whenever you go to boot it up, Steam says it's not made for a controller but you still can play it with the SC, so there is a bit of a disclaimer.
Games like Grim Dawn (a game like Torchlight or Diablo) make great use of the SC. It takes some getting used to because there are a few small extra steps, and you have to spend time configuring it to what you want, but the integration of the SC for Grim Dawn is near seamless. Although, I'm unaware if there's a button that lets pull up your skill tree map (I just resorted to pushing "S" on my keyboard).
Also with Grim Dawn, whenever I go to make a change in configuration for the SC, whenever I return to the game the SC doesn't work anymore, and I have to reboot the game to get it to work. It does at least keep your configuration change, but it seems like a problem.
How to map different actions to different buttons isn't made painfully obvious, and that's honestly what I would like.
But, I discovered, through tinkering that this is totally possible. It takes a little extra time to set up, but once you have it customized to what you want, it's primo.

While the customization options aren't painfully obvious, once you have them down, I can see this controller being the preferred option to other controllers.
For now, I'll recommend the SC. It is cheaper than many other controller options (good luck finding an XBOX 360 controller, and if you do, be ready to pay nearly $40 for it from GameStop: ebay has cheaper options though). Since I got it with the DS3 package, I paid about $35 for it, I'm beginning to feel that this is a fair price, once I learned how to map actions directly.
I see it available with some games as a package and I'd say go for it, but be prepared for the first person shooters to give you some trouble. Honestly, I'd still say wait for a special or deal, but I'm cheap.
I'll keep tinkering with it

I'd be willing to give this a higher rating, BUT I need to tinker with it in relation to first person shooters. With flight and driving sims, the gyro is a joystick/wheel and pedals minus the desk. Use the dual stage triggers to set as heavy and light ammunition types, to aim and shoot, to throttle/shift up and brake/shift down, etc. When away from the dest, my laptop trackpad never gets used for web browsing any longer. Soft pull the right trigger to activate gyro mouse, full pull trigger to LMB. Is it going to take some time to figure out what works for you, yes. Is it going to take some patiencs in your favorite compeditive online games to get up to speed, yes. Is the payoff the best gaming experiance you've ever had since the original gameboy, absolulely. 10/10 will fall in love again.

Pros:
- Beautiful Visuals. The paint-like art style has definitely allowed this game to age better than its spiritual predecessor Radiant Silvergun.
- Incredible Music. Every tune is lovely to my ears.
- Easy to learn, insanely hard to master gameplay. It's rather incredible just how many challenges Treasure's designers managed to squeeze out of the incredibly simple mechanics at play here, and it's awesome to see all the creative enemy designs they were able to make with them as well.
- Satisfying as all hell. Seriously, those explosions. I have never felt quite so good when killing a troublesome boss.
Cons:
- A menu annoyances. To my knowledge, once you select a game mode, you can't back out if you clicked something you didn't mean to. Effectively, you have to play a game and kill yourself or reset the game to get back to the title screen.
- No real explanation of the story. There is a plot to this game, and it's not an excuse plot. I won't devote time to explaining it here, but I do think it's quite a shame that there's no signs of the story in this port (again, to my knowledge).
- Chaining. I admit, I have never been a fan of this part of Ikaruga. While it's certainly nowhere near as bad as it was in Radiant Silvergun (There, you had to chain to upgrade your weapons, which was *essential* to defeating later bosses), I still don't particularly like a scoring system that effectively forces you to memorize everything that happens in an entire stage to hit those elusive S++ ranks. Granted, I'm also terrible at chaining, so take that as you will.
Overall, Ikaruga has earned its reputation as being one of the greatest shoot-'em ups ever made. Fantastic level design, creative boss designs, good story (in the versions that actually have it), great visuals and music. What else could you ask for?
Before I go, though, one word of warning:
While far from the hardest game in this genre, Ikaruga is still difficult. Like, really, really, really difficult. Dark Souls doesn't come close.
If you're not up for that, I would advise you avoid this game.

My second favorite game of this year. It manages to find the perfect balance between being friendly to newcomers while also being tough as hell for veterans. It's a metroidvania-genre game mixed up with touhou-like bullet hell. You control Erina, a bunny which somehow got transformed into a human, on your journey you will visit many various locations (each one with gr8 ost, btw), all of which are filled with various collectibles, power-ups, etc. You will often come across places which you can't access yet, since you need an extra ability for that, so here comes backtracking, which imo is pretty well done, it doesn't really force you to do it.
The main part of the game are boss encounters which are really well made. They do get tough, often covering the screen with projectiles through which you have to dodge your way, however they all seem to be pretty fair, and most of the time after few tries you will be able to easily dodge through enemy's bullet hell. I would recommend this game to anyone, in fact I have never played any metroidvanias or Touhou's etc. and I still had a lot of fun with this game. So overall, I'd say it's worth every penny for which it's priced. Same goes for ost, awesome piece of music.

The Dungeons series to me had first had quite the rocky start... I was looking for something to fix my dungeon making desires ever since the beloved DK of old. The Dungeons 1 however provided a completely different experience with quite an empty setting. The system of making your dungeon to the visitors needs before slaying them was an original concept, but not what I was after.
The sequel was met with some sceptical glance from me, but I saw they had picked up a heavy warcraft 3 tone for the war above ground and created a more functioning playful art style that though was parody to others in the genre, certainly looked better than the original games design. This direction was a more better experience and I had hours of fun with Dungeons 2 for its slower more relaxed pace of action. The expansion pack had a fun Game of Thrones parody and the new faction of undead was incredibly fun to play. Enjoyed everything it had to offer though like all parody game aspects the insults and gests can soon get outdated as the game goes on.
Dungeons 3... Now once again the parody element is clear and the direction so far is very fun! completed the first few levels and enjoying the cute themes of good getting crushed by evil. The game lacks identity in some respect but thats mainly down to the mish mash concepts of Warcraft and Dungeon Keeper blended with parodies from any popular fantasy movie/game. The dungeon building is solid and supplies many rooms, the team has been fleshed out to contain all the factions in one and makes me excited to think of how they will approach adding features in any DLC.
I have always enjoyed supporting the Dungeon series as I have only seen it get better as time goes on. The Co-Op Campaign makes playing this with a friend incredibly fun especially when both players prefer a more calm time-limit to the missions and working together at their own pace. I recommend this game to any fan of the Dungeon building genre or any of the RTS fans that want something fun and constructive without the stress of micro mangement.
All I can add is that perhaps some minor details to the graphics need to quickly get some polish and perhaps some of the rooms not look so complex. Less is more in most cases and detail works better when focused in areas rather than spread across the entire picture.
Looking forward to more from this game and more from the community playing it!

DOOM is a pretty freakin fantastic game. It's got a great story that can be easily ignored during second, third, or fourth playthroughs. The cutscenes (if you can call them that) last seconds at most and are far and few. However, in that short time, you can get this amazing world of demons and doomguys. The doomguy character in itself is amazing, the way he angrily reacts to Samuel Hayden's justification for the Argent Energy project (the one that caused this DOOM game, basically) tells an amazing story about your character, just by itself.
Aside from all the amazing story points this game has, it's actual playability is even better. There is nothing more cathartic than literally ripping in half a demon before doing a 360 and punching another one's head so hard it explodes. The difficulty levels are the first ones I've ever used in a game, because as time went on I actually got better at it. As of now, I've completed a nightmare run, a pistol-only run, every other difficulty run, and one kinda special run where you don't upgrade any weapons or your suit. They were all great.
Honestly I'm not sure why it says I have so few hours on DOOM. It feels like my most played game of 2017, and even though so far I don't have 2x the money cost in hours (which is my general rule for a good game), DOOM is definitely worth it.

I’ve been playing this game for years and while it does have some underlying issues that are constantly being worked on, tweaked and updated, are not deal-breakers by any means.
My suggestion for any new people who know very little about either the BattleTech or MechWarrior franchise is to take a look at the in-game forums (especially the New Player Guides). The information present there will be very helpful in getting you started and navigating the game’s (somewhat steep at times) learning curve…though you should also take care as well, there’s a very salty group of veterans in there as well. While many of them may of them mean well, they can come across very angry. These people do not necessarily have to be avoided; just take what these guys say with a grain of salt. Even then, there are plenty of other players and veterans who are more than willing to help newcomers who are a LOT less rough around the edges.
This all being said, the game is a very good game…but not Triple A by any means (though it doesn’t pretend that it’s trying to be…despite the comparisons some people keep trying to make). Despite that, the gameplay is complex and diverse when it comes down to ‘Mech construction (and there are a LOT of customization options!), and no match will ever be played the say way twice.
My suggestion for new players is to make use of the MechWarrior Academy and all of its different features; this will help you learn a good portion of what you need to know and when you’re ready, pick up a trial ‘Mech and have fun. You will get a significant bonus to your in-game money (called C-Bills) for your first 25 games which should put you well on the road to picking up your first, fully customizable BattleMech.

Let's break this down into several components. Gameplay, UI, Graphics, Content, End Game.
Gameplay 8/10:
This game down to its core is a very fun game when you play it and learn it. Its an action shooter but it doesn't have the cartoon speed of some other FPS where you die after stubbing your toe on a bullet. No you can take a hit and if you are smart can survive for as long as you can. There's a sense of tactics in there somewhere. It's knowing when to attack, when to retreat, when to work with your team. You don't just run and gun and respawn.
That is just half the game to launch into a match though. The second half is to make and create your own mech builds. To be able to tinker and change a chassis to how you want to play and not some stock loadout. To own and change every mech that you can get. To collect and master all the mechs you want provided you get the mechbays you need.
It isn't perfect, balance could be better in regards to lesser used weapons. There could be more balance between the two major 'Factions' the Clans and the Inner Sphere.
Overall it feels like a fun game to play,
UI 7/10:
The first incarnation was terrible, the second incarnation horrific, and now we have this current '2.5' UI that has honestly been a success. There's a lot of clicking but in comparison to other games like say Armoured Warfare it isn't actually as bad as it use to be. A lot of information that needs to be presented to you is but there is room for improvement which will come.
What the game needs? UI Tooltips when you work in the Mechlab. UI for Mech Modules (Extra addons for mechs), and just quality of life improvements.
Overall the UI is not special but its not terrible.
Graphics 8/10:
Mechwarrior: Online is showing its age. It runs on a outdated engine that has high demands for less gains. We've seen the power and scale of CryEngine 3 as a FPS but it demands much more when you see 12 vs 12 Giant mechs that take up a lot more power to render. The graphics are however still quite amazing. The visuals of seeing your lasers, cannons, and missiles fire is amazing. You won't be disappointed by all the effects.
However you would want optimizations out of this game. It definitely needs to be optimized across the board.
Overall its a great visual overall but it isn't the type of visuals you would expect from some triple AAA title which you shouldn't anyways.
Content 8/10:
In my opinion the story is not rich but the lore behind it is. It leads into having a lot of room for content in the future. It already has hundreds of mechs to choose from which is the meat of the content. There's so much room for variety that it provides so much content already. Could it have more than just mechs? Yes.
I want to see more than just PvP Matches. It lacks in content that isn't just PvP.
Overall its still good but that leads into the last component.
End Game 5/10:
The end game is unfinished. Plain and Simple it is not done. It is an interesting Idea of a moving world but it just seems like a map and place to fight right now.
The future looks bright for it with new modes of play, the ability to use guild/faction/unit money to buy things with but its not there yet.
_________
Overall this game is 7.5/10 until more patches come out. I have some faith but it needs to be proven at this point.

Oh right! Review! Kinda Important!
In case you want the short version: At the point of the game that I'm at now, I rate it a 9.5/10.
2 hours into the game (the Refund limit) I give it an 8/10. The reason for the change is in the longer verison.
A balance of gameplay and challenge that never gets too easy no matter how you do things. That's a rare thing these days, and most of the time when it's attempted, it's a fantastic piece of crap. Thankfully, I don't need to say that this game follows suit. It's fun, fast paced, and challenges me throughout the game (so far). It's not too grindy on a normal play though and it's not the worse when it comes to cramming fanservice down your throat, which surprised me, to say the least. The Music has something for almost everyone, from old classic video game music to decent Electro. Best part is, I can't think of a single theme that drove me insane or annoyed me.
Breakdown: ("2 hours in" rating - "Current, 7.1 hours in" rating) (Both ratings are out of 10 before someone asks....)
Gameplay: (9 - 9.5)
Gameplay was a little weird at first. You lack any weapons, and can acutally miss the weapon if you ignore it or pass it by. After you get the weapon, you lack any upwards air attack (you get a down-air attack rather shortly after swinging the hammer a few times) or dash attacks. This was my mistake in thinking this game was merely a Hack-n-slash. About 30-50 minutes in the game, your main source of attacks finds you, and then the game starts to come together.
After my second boss, I realised how I should have taken this game as: A bullet hell with hack-n-slash in the mix as an option. Sounds bad, but oddly enough, it works out really well. A nearly seemless mix of the two fighting styles. Grinding is nearly non-existent in a normal run, as you level by buying powerups for items (which you don't "need" to do, but it helps) or by hitting things a bunch of times (it was so quick I maxed my magic related stuff before hitting the 4th boss. You get magic after the 2nd boss).
As far as non-combat gameplay goes, it's got loads of the famous MetroidVania traits: Tiered Exploration/ Progression, Secrets galore, and plenty of powerups.  And it's got it's own flare to it, which makes the exploring part less annoying. Sadly, it is that retracing aspect that hits this game for me, but .5/10 isn't such a bad hit. Teleporters thankfully are more functional and user-friendly (that's the long way of saying "better") than, say.... Dust: AET with the Teleport stones and area select.
Visuals: (10 - 9.5)
Nothing much to say on this. I knew what to expect in game. But I was really impressed with the menus. The main menu was clean and didn't have any annoying fluff while still looking nice. The in-game pause menu was a sight for sore eyes, as everything was there in clear cut sections. This is to be expected in a video game, but it was a breath of fresh are for me after playing some games that managed to mess that up. I gave it a .5 reduction in my current rating because of the slighly over the top fanservice at times, but it's not bad enough to warrent a big concern, as more times than not, it adds to the story or character(s) quite well.
Music: (9 - 10)
My lord, I haven't been this hooked to a soundtrack since Undertale. One thing this soundtrack does better than Undertale is how they mix it quite a bit more. I enjoyed all 13 boss themes I've been in so far, and a lot of these songs pumped me up for the fight, while still seeming to make it match the personallity of the boss your fighting, or of the reason your fighting the boss. None of the overworld themes are bad either. Couldn't really complain about anything at the 4 hour mark, making it a perfect score for me at that point.
Story: (6 - 9)
REALLY confusing start to the game, with almost none of it explained within the first 2 hours. There's the UPRPRC thing that confused the heck outta me until the 3 hour mark, where it all made sense afterwards. At the 4 hour mark, most of what happened in the begining is at least brushed upon slightly several times, which gives me hope on the story. Each Character within the town has a story or three of their own too. Each one helps add meaning behind that character and any related characters, which is a plus. However, holes galore on that front too. I still give it a 9 now because of how well the story's holes are being filed right now. It's still slightly on the "blah" side of stories, but the story itself is well presented in a rather charming way.
Replayability/ Enjoyment: (6 - 9)
Two hours in, your kinda stuck on rails. I feared that this game may be a case that "Non-linear" meant that you could fight one boss or the other first. What I'm glad to find out is that "other" was not the correct word when saying that. "Others" is the correct word in that statement and you can fight a few of them before continuing the main story, and there is a few optional areas and minigames too.
Boss battles are fair, and if it's too easy, you can up the settings after you hit town, and lower the setting ONCE if it's too hard for you. Dying in a boss battle isn't frustrating, as it loads you into the room before the boss, and you generally aren't boss-trapped in a save lock (unless you stick with Auto save, which is dumb of you if you do. Cat girl blocks your path to a real save, and the rest of the map, in an optionalish area, thanks to auto save. Use Auto save as an "Oh no, power died" avoidence, not a full save coverage. Tip of the day.) The combat gets better rather fast, about 4 hours in and I love all that combat has to offer, and new skills are added quite often to spice up the first run. Mastering the skills... now that's the fun part as all the skills have hidden uses that make them all better after you learn them and the game never really points it out. That makes the game way more fun and engaging to me as a player.
Replayability is very high, with 5 difficulty modes, along with no item, no hammer, no health upgrade, and speedrun modes/goals to spice up gameplay. There's even a post game, as i've learned, that can hopefully adds even more to the enjoyment and replayability.
Overall (8 - 9.5)
Story and Enjoyment kinda kills the first two hours, but once your free to do whatever your abilities and your personal skills within the game will take you, things get really fun, and more of the lore and world are offered to you. I'm glad that the begining was more poor than the rest of the game. So many games make an amazing opening and then fall on their face halfway in. This game doesn't have that problem.
IS IT WORTH THE BASE PRICE OF $17.99?
Yeah, I say it pays it's dues nicely. Kinda surprised it isn't more.

Deus EX: Human Revolution is an enjoyable and compelling game with an interesting story and decent gameplay. There is content for quite a while and situations can be approached in different ways.
Condensed list of the good and the bad, mostly arranged by personal experience:
The game is enjoyable, but has some noticable flaws in the gameplay.
is the major offender with
sprint, poor strafing capabilities, fiddly jumping mechanic and needlessly prompted actions (such as moving from cover to cover, around a cover and climbing) accompanied by awkward cutscenes (Icarus Landing System).
is enjoyable and as stated earlier, the multiple approaches available offer a commendable value to the gameplay. Direct, long range and hidden assaults are all viable options with each having a lethal and non-lethal variety.

One downside in Deus Ex: HR's combat is the melee system. Unlike the previous game(s), HR does not have melee weapons that can be equipped like other equipment, but instead you are given prompts every time you are near an enemy. This activates a cutscene where you use your arms to knock the target(s) unconscious or kill them.
Activating the prompt uses an energy cell, which limits the melee use further.
is one of the few things that feel just spot on with variety of large and small weapons, each offering their own characteristics.
[Edit] There are also minor bugs to be expected.
In comparison to the first game in the franchise (Deus Ex), the freedom of movement is much more limited. Certain cutscenes, Icarus Landing System for example tug you right out of the game. The greatest strengths of Deus Ex: HR are its story and dialogue in addition to combat and gunplay.
HR could be described as a good B-movie; an enjoyable experience with its own flaws.

You may have seen this game as Canis Canem Edit. It received a lot of flak for being called "Bully" in some parts of the word.
You could play the main character as a straight up bully if you wanted, but you wouldn't progress very far through the main storyline if you did.
If our hero, Jimmy, is a bully - then so are all the heroes from Westerns: He defends the weaker kids AGAINST bullies (if you play it in the manner it was designed to be played), by bullying the bullies (insert bullyception joke HERE).
You could say this is 'Grand Theft Auto for kids', and you wouldn't really be wrong. Teens, not youngsters. If you're a bit of a prude, like I am.
It bears all the hallmarks of the GTA series: A main storyline that's not so much controversial as it is silly, with plenty of vehicles, costumes, and subgames, and the worst part of the game is, by far, the sluggish and counter-intuitive combat mechanics.
And as a person that rarely had a positive experience at so-called 'school', this was a great way for me to work through that. And was heaps cheaper than a therapist.
(I'm only mostly joking about that.)
You can kiss girls (and boys, for those so inclined) to recharge your health. I only wish this game had been around when I was younger, and kissing young girls (even digital ones) didn't feel creepy for me. I kept looking around for Chris Hansen.
You can skateboard around the place, or ride a bike when you get one. You can also eventually unlock a motorcart/GoKart.
The only things I really don't like about this game are the combat (it's okay, it's just too strategic, and therefore too slow, for what I would *personally* like to see) and the fact that some of the school minigames require me to put my gamepad down and use the mouse, because of the way they're designed/coded - I am looking directly at you, 'science class'.
Things to note:
- Completionists should do some research before they play - some stuff is missable.
- The combat is okay, I just don't dig on it. But it's neither 'outright crappy' nor 'totally pointless'.
- In one of the missions, you had to do a panty raid. I still don't know how I feel about that. Wait, yes I do: Icky. (see also: kissing girls for health)
In closing, I'd like to say that this was, by far, the most GTA style fun I ever had until I discovered my favourite open world series (which I won't mention here).
I would recommend this to anyone who wants to try their kids out on a GTA style game without any of the crude humor associated with it. There IS crude humour in the game, but it's either pitched at or well above kids. I can imagine people replaying this years later and thinking: "I can't believe I didn't understand that properly when I was younger."
I would also recommend it to anyone who likes GTA but hasn't played this game. It's not 'the same' but it should scratch the GTA itch, even if only for a few hours.

I would totally recommend the Steam Controller purely for the rebindability functions alone - this and the back buttons make for a mostly fluid, enjoyable gaming experience, perfect for when you're in the living room.

This is a very good product. For a while, I'd had a bit of trouble with some games that are much better when used with controllers. For example, Dark Souls (1 and 2), Shadows of Mordor, Warhammer 40K: Space Marine, Spec Ops: The Line, and Bioshock Infinte work much better with a controller. Note that 3 of the above are what some would call Shooters. The Mouse-and-Keyboard combo works less well with games of that sort. Not that you cannot play them, but it can be harder. Shadows of Mordor is easier with a controller because there are a lot of contextual buttons prompts. It can be hard to execute a Brutalize stealth attack without a controller because the same button for "Brutalize" is the same one for Stealth Kill and Select, and without a controller the button prompts (press "Y" to Brutalize) do not appear as often (or at all) with just Mouse-and-Keyboard.
What I am trying to say, is that the Steam Controller is an excellent way to play console games on your laptop, especially if you do not own an Xbox and can use its controller.
I purchased this some time around February. I have only had to change its batteries once since then, and I play 1-5 hours per day. It is definately something even a casual gamer can use and enjoy, because it enhances the quality of certain playthroughs.
Pros:
Good battery life.
Comes with a cord and a wireless connector, so you can pick and mix which is more your style.
Controls and commands can be customized and certain configurations work best with different games.
More games on Steam are becoming compatible with the controller.
Works with most Triple A games that have come out recently.
You can use the Steam controller with any game on Steam, just note that some (Like the Total War and Civ series) are not traditionally played with controllers, and thus are more conditioned towards Mouse-and-Keyboard play styles.
Cons:
Some older Steam games do not work well with the Steam Controller. Fallout: New Vegas for example does not crossover well, and Fallout 3 is similar. They do not show the controller's button prompts and only refer to the Keyboard shortkeys.
The Trackpad is very sensitive, and you will want to adjust it as soon as possible, or else you can end up swinging the camera about wildly with just a nudge.
Some games may work better when using Big Picture, which is also an important feature to use when adjusting and modding the Steam Controller.
Overall, the Steam Controller is worth the price. Somewhat expensive at nearly $50, but worth it.

Megadimension Neptunia VII is the 4th main title in the "Hyperdimension" series. Following the events of Re;Birth: 3 the main cast goes on their biggest adventure yet. This time we follow the tragic tale of the Sega Dreamcast.
If you've played any of the previous games you'll know what to expect going in. A large cast, lots  of meta jokes, hundreds upon hundreds of jokes about Gamer and Otaku culture, and a turn-based battle system that rewards mild positioning and strategy. but lacks real depth. If you've been following the Video Game scene for a while expect to get about 1/2 the jokes. If you know a lot of Otaku culture (Anime, 2Chan, etc.) expect to get the other half.
PROS:
CONS:
OVERALL:
While I can't call this one the best of the main series, I still think 3 is the overall best, it is definitely up there. If you want to try the series out for the first time I'd recommend checking Re;Birth 3 out over this one. It's simply a better entry point for the series. Megadimension Neptunia takes the series 3 steps forward and 1 step back. I'd love to see Quests be more important and the development tab return to form. As it stands it is still a very good game, but it isn't a great game.

I picked up the Neptunia series a little less than four months ago, and I have to say--this is the best one out of all the games that I've played yet. Although I've barely scratched the surface, I am loving what I am seeing so far. It is on the path to becoming a favourite vidya of mine. I'd highly recommend this: it's as close as you will get to finding a 'perfect game'.
Pros/Cons I have noticed so far:
(+): Running on a somewhat dated AMD graphics card and processor (absolutely disgusting, I know) in 45-60fps and high video quality. This is impressive given how I could not do this with Re;Birth 1 or 2--a good testament to how this is a pretty good modern port.
(+): Continuity of certain relationships/certain arcs of the earlier games. It's suffice to say that this latest edition restores/retains many of the relationships from the previous games (my favorite, Nep and Noire; the sisters; Nepgear and Uni; etc). It also retains the elements of story people may have liked from 1 or 2, while not necessarily retconning or confirming others. It just leaves controversial parts of certain previous games unmentioned. In my opinion, this is a good take on how to deal with loose ends [unresolved arcs] when adding a new game to your series.
(+): Pretty effective new chars.; pretty effective perosnas for each one.
(+): One of the first things I noticed is that the dialogue is much less long-winded than the
previous games. The conversations featured in the game convey their main point concisely, and even manage to add some filler into each one without feeling superfluous.
(+): Holds many clever parallels and/or references to the first game which I certainly enjoyed. This undoubtedly holds some significance to the story, too.
(+): Impressive visuals comparative to other games in the series, and in general. I particularly enjoyed what they did with the character models during conversation scenes. Compile Heart REALLY committed to sharpening the models of each character, and I love it.
(+): Like the previous games, this holds a metric♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of fan service. But you're probably well aware of this, too, if you are browsing this series in the first place.
(+): Kick♥♥♥♥♥musical score
(+): Glorious yuri overload
(+): Large, original, and fairly pretty maps/reskins. I'm around 15% in, and its 75% original; 25% reskin.
(biggest pro/con): There is no fourth wall. Take that as you will.
(minor con): Takes a while for the story to officially ignite. It took around 40 minutes for me to become fully engaged.
I'll come back to this and edit as I progress with the story.
Update: True Ending improves the game A LOT. I was already really satisifed and considering it a favorite game of mine even with a lesser ending. After that though, I'd say I'm satisifed enough to 100% this game, which I generally never do with games. Additionally, the prerequisites to achieving it are less convoluted or understated compared to the previous games. I think fans of the series like myself will be very happy with it.
