I noticed I have not done a review for this game. I shall now do one like I usually do with previous Nep games! :3
Normally, I would write a chunk in my review but this time, I'll "try" to summarise it overall. Personally, Megadimension Neptunia VII is probably the best installment so far for the series along with RB1 and RB3 as my favourites. I'm actually surprised that despite the minimum requirements, I am able to run this on a Surface Pro 3. However, the newer dungeons, Dark CPU, NEXT Forms and animations for skills/EXEs were rather laggy. Everything else ran suitably enough to play. There are still a bunch of re-used dungeons from previous games but that does not matter. Monsters seem to be different, more variety and some are re-colours. In regards to gameplay, I liked how they tried to make it more challenging in a way such as the one dungeon with no map and only those in battle get EXP which may cause underlevels for some late game. I quite liked the hidden treasures, figurine/card collector achievements. It gives the game a new touch for not being as repetitive. Uniquely, I think they were also added to balance out the grindy achievements such as the good ol' classic lily rank achievements we've been getting the past installments which are much easier to max in VII. I liked the new soundtrack, the CG that is avaiable and reading the events to know more about the characters. One memorable one I'm quite fond of is the matching hats event between Histy and Uzume ^^ Other miscellaneous things I liked were the costumes and accessories, in particular IF and Compa as they finally have another outfit!
Would I nepping recommend this? If you're a nep fan, played a previous nep game then yes. If you're new I'd say, give it a go! Though I'm not sure if you should start with this one. Personally I would say to try RB1 to know what this game is about and it's concept. If not, then start with RB3 ^^

Dungeons 3 eh ? .... where shall we start. 8/10
WHAT IS DUNGEONS 3
Dungeons 3 is a strategy game inspired by the cult classic dungeon keeper franchise by bullfrog (RIP Bullfrog).
The game takes some classic gameplay from dungeon keeper such as digging out your dungeon, building rooms, gathering \ training your minions and finally laying traps for those pesky hero's. It also becomes its own game adding the overworld combat that was teased for Dungeon keeper 3. When in the overworld your armies take on a totaly new role where the games goes from a dungeon keeper style game too a sort of warcraft 3 style game where you can micro your minions activate there abilities and so on.
If you want a more true to the original game I could not recomend a game called "war for the overworld" any more both are wonderfull games. You can find "War for the Overworld* here :
Now back to Dungeons 3 ....
THE PRO'S
The game feels true enough to the dungeon keeper series too scratch that itch for keeper fans but also its different enough to be its own game and a new experience.
The game has a great sense of humor and lots of refrences that makes me cackle.
The variety from the underworld to the overworld helps keep the gameplay fresh. You can spend a long time building up your lair, go for a walk for a change of pace then spend the next half hour useing traps to kill of those invading hero's
Graphics are quite nice + go well with the not taking its self serious feel of the game.
Gameplay is basic enough to pick up fast but complicated enough to give depth. For example you can just yolo charge your army or you can move your minions around to avoid damage, toggle and activate abilities focus healers and the list goes on and on and those where for just a small combat in the overworld.
The research tree is easy to understand and quite fun with enough areas to spec into to give you quite a bit of variety and playstyles. The resources needed to advance your research also forced you to advance in the overworld not just the underworld so you cant just build up then steamrole. as someone who often does build up and steam role i am glad its not the best option as it breaks up the gameplay and helps everything feel fresh.
The User interface ( for most of the game ) is very well done and easy to understand.
THE CON'S
The in-level user interface menu on the left side of the screen is a wee bit annoying and takes some time getting used too. It took me a long time too stop summoning new minions when i was trying to select ones I already had. The tab for your army is also not bad when you do not have too many minions but as soon as you have more than 5 it becomes hard too organise clustered and a pain in the backside to find the minion you want and impossible to do so with any speed.
I miss portals spawning minions.
THE END
Thanks for your time reading this and i hope it helped you make up your mind if you wanted to purchase the game :)

I had an ABSOLUTE BLAST playing this with my friends! We had some really intense 1 on 1 matches that were so much fun. It's one of those games with such a satisfying amount of skill that every time you win you or lose, once you are done shouting in triumph telling your your friend to "Eat It!" or shouting in rage that you lost such a close match, your immediate reaction is to play again. When there's lots of laughing and shouting going on, that's a great co-op game. And there was definitely plenty of that when we played.
There is a surprising amount of depth to master in the nuance of the timing and controls of the various combat and movement mechanics. The amount of focus on movement; dancing, dodging, and juking your opponent(s) definitely reminds me of Super Smash Bros.
I played through the entire Solo story mode and was actually pretty impressed with the serious, but fair challenge that the AI provided. I found myself mashing the "Rematch" button every time that I lost to my friends or the AI.

[Edit:] After I just played another hidden object game, I just realized that the map feature which does not only show you where you might be able to do something at a certain time, but also allows you to quick travel and therefore save you from spending much time just moving from location to location, is woth mentoining as an additional positive point. [/edit]
A beautiful extra is that you can replay any hidden object screens and puzzles and rewatch all video sequences once you have finished the game.
Well, most reviews I write are much longer, but there realy isn't much to say. So: If you are fan of hidden object games, this is a recommendation. If you just want to waste some hours with a decent time killer game, I'd wait for a discount.

Review by Ainslie (my partner, a fan of hidden object games)
It is quite rare to find me glued to a computer game for more than 20 minutes at a time, but from the instant I started The Secret Order 2: Masked Intent I couldn’t seem to get enough.  I kept working for the next goal, finish the next puzzle and find the next clue.  I loved the combination of adventure, hidden object games and mini puzzles, each linking cohesively with the next.  The story brings to life a world of magic, mysticism and history that leaves you wanting to know what happens next and has you invested in defeating each challenge that stands in your way. I found the graphics to be perfect for the game as they had an antique feel but are also colorful and engaging without being garish which some games in the genre can be. I enjoyed the cut scenes and the dialogue which were appropriately timed and were succinct enough to not take away from the playing of the game. The cut scenes can be entirely skipped if you so choose, but the story is a good one for the genre so I would recommend that you watch them to keep immersed in the game.
If you are a fan of hidden object games and like a great story line and extra challenges thrown in to make the game oh so better then this is the game for you.  Personally i can’t wait to get Warwick out of his game account to I can finally complete my first game.  Enjoy!

A daring adventure through time with magic, ghosts, dragons and family drama; this game is filled to the brim with excitement from beginning to end.
A good story is what keeps me playing games like these. I enjoy following along with the main character and helping them to complete their mission. This tale revolves around Sara who is trying to save her parents from her very own brother. Along the way she discovers a time traveling ship and goes to the past to uncover the mystical artifact that will defeat the darkness.
While the story is good, it drags a bit to me. The time traveling aspect wasn’t as exciting as it sounds on paper. You only go to one time period and, of course, do mundane tasks until you finally get the information you need...THEN you get sucked into a vortex of some sorts and have to defeat two evil specters to escape. This part, I believe, is added content for the collector’s edition to make it longer which might explain why it seems out of place from the rest of the story. However, once back on track to finding the scepter things pick up pace again.
Gameplay is common fair for this genre of game. You have plenty of hidden object scenes, I wouldn’t even have minded more. You also have plenty of puzzles, some frustrating but the instructions are clear and you can get past them without having to skip. If you’re playing on Steam, gaining all of the achievements should not be difficult. The game also offers a mahjong alternative if you can’t find an item during a hidden object scene.
Artwork is beautiful, though the characters suffer from dead eyes during cut scenes when they look at it. It’s a bit creepy but nothing too distracting. The soundtrack is great at setting the tone of the game and smooth on the ears along with talented voice acting.
As of the time I’m writing this review, the first installment of this series is not on Steam yet. I would love to see it and more stories involve the Order of the Gryphon available, however. The mythos of the game is intriguing and a lot of mystical fun.

Deus Ex Human Revolution - Director’s Cut Review
Introduction:
Deus Ex HRDC is a first person shooter with RPG elements, set in the near future in a world where chaos and conspiracy are rife. The majority of the game is free roam and the choices you make during the game will effect the world around you. Based before the original Deus Ex you are placed in the role of Adam Jensen an ex-swat team member, who now finds him self in charge of security for one of the largest biotechnology firms in America.
Story:
The Deus games have always been driven on conspiracy theory’s, Human Revolution is no different. All through the game you will be questioning who to trust and who not to, friends may become enemiesand enemies friends. The story really does a great job of keeping you suspicious, your never sure if your a good guy or a bad one. Add to that some of the choices the game gives you with no clear moral option, you’ll find yourself constantly second guessing yourself.
But the story does feel rushed at times and some questions it rises never really feel answered, some moments feel unexplained. In fact if you turn the commentary on in extras they them selves will tell you they ran out of time to fully realize all they wanted to do. Its a shame as it really does show, But what’s there is good and achieves exactly what they were trying to.
Gameplay:
As of late I’ve been struggling to get in to FPS games as the market is so saturated, but Deus Ex HRDC does truly offer something different from the norm. The controls are a pretty standard fair with one or two odd key placements, but nothing that hampers the experience. But its the augmentations that really put this game apart, some being basic things like faster sprinting or improving hacking skills. But its the stealth augments and things like punching through walls that really make this fun, and stealth is a big element of Deus. Its possible if your careful and cleaver to get through almost every mission without firing a shot, but at times you will probably have to so lucky even your weapons are upgradeable too.
If I have one major criticism of the gameplay, its the cover system. When you take cover or use a take down move you move into 3rd person view, this is great for a visual effect but feels really jarring in practice. It just doesn’t flow right and left me feeling like they should have ether made the whole game in 3rd person or found a way to do it in 1st person. Even the option like Skyrim where you can use ether view I would have welcomed over the way its executed here, I also feel that FPS vets will probably not use the cover system anyway.
Presentation:
The graphics are great for a 2 year old game and really do give that futuristic atmosphere. Some maps do feel like your walking down the same corridor fifteen times as there all so similar, but this is to be expected. Thankfully most levels are in more open settings with a wider verity of surroundings. There at times is a almost Blade Runner feel to the game, this is really emphasized by the neon lit menus and displays in the game. The character models are great too, with every character seeming unique and fresh.
Conclusion:
I really enjoyed Deus, more than I thought I would. If your looking for something a little deeper than the standard FPS then really look no farther. With a deep plot that to me seem heavily inspired by the works of Isaac Asimov and gameplay that’s a little different I found it a real breath of fresh air. There’s really not a lot here not to like and I would recommend it highly to anyone into FPS games.

After waking up as a human, Rabi has to go on a quest around the island she lives on to gather magic users to try and rescue Miru. Early on in this quest, she meets a fairy named Ribbon. Through the whole thing, you'll be greeted with a fairly enjoyable story, although it does sometimes just come in large chunks spread out across the map.
Rabi-Ribi is a Metroidvania bullet hell game that will really challenge you. It features numerous difficulties, and even with playing the game on Novice (the lowest one), I still had some bosses I struggled against. With being a Metroidvania, expect to be doing a lot of backtracking as you unlock new abilities and gain access to precious inaccessible areas. There's a lot to collect and find as well, so if you're a completionist, expect to spend a long time on this game.
Overall, I enjoyed Rabi-Ribi quite a lot. I did feel that the "larger" sprites (IE: when you're under the Giant debuff) looked a bit poor, and I did spot a few grammar mistakes. However, despite all that, Rabi-Ribi is a very enjoyable game if you enjoy either Metroidvania or bullet hell games. If you're looking for a game that will give you plenty to do, and will also give you a nice (and sometimes frustrating) challenge, then I'd definitely suggest looking into the game. If you're on the fence about it and feel like the $18 price tag might be a bit too high for you, I'd suggest waiting for a sale and getting it then.

So what can I say about this game? It was my favorite game of 2016 by a long shot, and I actually mean that.
I feel like everyone's afraid of making anything "cute" anymore. At the very least, it's really hard to find anything that unashamedly embraces the aesthetic, and you really only find this kind of game coming from the east, which I think is kind of a shame. Over here it feels like everything has to eat beef jerky and♥♥♥♥♥♥the skulls of its enemies. Anything cute has to be directly marketed at girls because only GIRLS could like cute things and if it uses cute girls to that end that aren't more modestly covered than "business casual" it's sexist garbage.
I think what made me fall in love with this game is how unashamedly it just
. It's a quality that's hard to define, but one that I feel is absent from most games. The cute aesthetic is worked into every facet of the entire game, including some of the most mundane parts of the UI. This game doesn't just wants to show you cute, it wants to smother you with cute, it wants to drown you in the cute. There's so much aversion to actual cute nowadays that you half expect that it's going to pull an eversion and pull a "SUDDENLY SPOOKS WHAT A TWEEEEEEST" but it never does. It's so unrelentingly sacharine that I can't help but love it. it's a game that, if nothing else, feels utterly sincere. I don't feel that often in any media, it always feels like most of what I see is build from the ground up to market towards some broad demographic group brainstormed in a boardroom somewhere. In a world where it feels more and more like everything either panders to that or to pseudo-intellectuals high on their own farts, a game like this feels like a breath of fresh air.
Even the gameplay doesn't really follow conventions. This is a cross between a metroidvania and a bullet hell. You don't see that every day, and it pulls it off fantastically. It is a total blast to play. If you like platforming combat and dodging lots of bullets, this game does it very well. Outside of this, maps are littered with hidden upgrades and pickups to collect, a lot of it gated off by needing other powerups first(classic metroidvania design). The only downside I feel I can give it is that outside of boss fights combat often feels kind of easy and mundane, but it's not too much of a detriment. I think this could have been helped by throwing in mini-boss enemies to break up the flow.
The music is some of the best I've heard in a game. I'm no musician or music reviewer so I can't really tell you how rattly the high-hats are or whatever, but it sounds absolutely amazing and I'd recommend at least giving it a listen The spritework looks really good, and the full-size portraits look alright, my only nitpick there being they look a little dolljointed and the color pallette doesn't quite match the tones of the sprites, but that's a mere nitpick. Everything else of the illustrations look fantastic.
Finally, the one downside. This game has framerate issues. Bad. If you have a pre-built computer made in the past two years, you should be fine. Same goes for any gaming PC from the past 5. Beyond that, you will likely come across framerate issues because this game is a freaking unoptimized resource hog. I have the PS4 version and the framerate issues even show up there to an extent.
Honestly, I can't recommend this game enough. It is my favorite game of 2016 and worth every cent of its price. on top of everything else it has a high replay value, with plenty of difficulty modes and challenges like the no-items run. Go out and get it, it's a truly amazing game.

---- Original Review ----
I'll be the first to write a somewhat negative review about this game:
First: I started playing this game around 2006-07, prior to Retail Blockland's (the current game) release. This game is almost entirely community-based. This game is what you want to make it, which means the community needs responsible, creative users to help form a fun game for everyone.
This has been a problem since the recent removal of maps, which were an easy way to play the game without putting too much effort into it. Currently, the game has a lack of creative players which have caused many, many players to quit the game due to the lack of content from the developer (which he removed maps with a promise of more content, which never came, even a year later), and the lack of decent servers to play on.
However, Blockland has always had the problem of a small community which has made decent servers scarce. The lack of maps has left mapmakers without their ability to contribute to Blockland, causing them to leave along with many other players who enjoyed playing on maps rather than the default (and now, the only) map, "Slate".
I'm not going to lie. I, and many others have felt that the game has been dead (or dying) for a long time now. Even when maps were still here, the game was dying slowly, but surely -- the removal of the maps just kickstarted it because nobody knew how to cope with the lack of creative builders to replace the position that maps once held.
Steam, for some of us, is believed to be the last resort for Blockland's future. It's up to you, the newest purchaser who is reading this review, to help reform the community into something better, more active, and more stable.
Another problem is that since the maps were removed, many players with low-spec computers were forced to quit due to being unable to process the amount of bricks it would take to create a "map".
So, if you've got a low-spec PC, I would not recommend this game to you until you get a computer with a decent processor and graphics card. Otherwise, you'll be playing with a constant lag that will drive you to hate the game.
The shaders are poorly optimized. (And I mean, they are *extremely* poorly optimized.) So the majority of the Blockland community don't even play with the shaders that we sacrificed our maps for because they can't even run them. Not even high-spec computers can run the shaders with a large amount of bricks unless you've got a ridiculously powerful computer. I've got a quad-core i5 processor and an AMD 7870 Graphics card, 2GB video memory, and I can run Battlefield 3 on max settings with over 60FPS, whereas I have trouble running shaders on max in Blockland and end up only getting around 28-30FPS with builds that are around 50k bricks or more.
The gameplay is good as long as you play on a decent server, it depends on your tastes.
I'm also going to warn anyone who buys this game: Prepare to be flamed, trolled, or annoyed by the community at some point. The game has one of the most merciless, rude, arrogant communities I have ever been a part of. However, that's not the majority of the community. A lot of the community is very nice and like to take part with each other in building projects or film-making and such. But if you ask me, the community needs an increase in better players.
To conclude, we have a lack of a decent, creative playerbase right now and we need more players with more creativity and will to step forward and create something awesome out of this game. Everything in the trailer IS possible, but most of it has never happened and will never happen unless we have more creative players. The trailer was highly exaggerated and the game is far more boring than that. But like I said, everything in the trailer is possible, but it hasn't happened -- yet.
So, if you're willing to be a good player and you want to help revive an almost-dead game and form it into a better game for everyone's enjoyment, buy the game. If you don't want to work with the community, hate playing games that take time and effort to make something good out of it, or just generally dislike overhyped games, don't buy it. Even though the game is overexaggerated, it doesn't mean we can't work together to make it that awesome.
It's up to you.

text:
Ikaruga is a shmup by Treasure - a company known for classics like Mischief Makers, Alien Solider, Gunstar Heroes, Gradius V (on Konami's behalf), and spiritual (and possibly direct) prequel Radiant Silvergun.
Gameplay is extremely solid. At it's most basic, Ikaruga puts you in control of the titular ship, which has two abilities - you can shoot, and you can change the Ikaruga's polarity. The polarity mechanic works thusly: Enemies are color-coded, and you're immune to projectiles color-coded from enemies which share your present color. This may sound simple on paper, but the game is a bullet hell with little tolerance for failure. Staying alive is a constant struggle and requires unfaltering attention as well as considerable ability to sort out visual noise, so this isn't a good choice for those in the mood for an easy play. Those familiar with Treasure will know that their games are often incredibly simple yet exceedingly difficult and often expect complete mastery of mechanics to progress; Ikaruga certainly carries on the tradition. The game rewards several different approaches to play and has a bevy of settings, providing replay value in droves.
Those who do well enough may find themselves butting heads with a certain stony foe from a previous Treasure game...
Visual and sound design are stellar, with compelling enemy designs and an excellently composed score by composer Hiroshi Iuchi. The spartan black and white design motifs further emphasize (and almost feel like an extention of) the game's mechanics, and the music certainly makes me feel like the last survivor of a botched rebellion going solo against an empire with the power of a god behind it.
All-in-all, Ikaruga's not going to be everyone's cup of tea since it's an incredibly hectic game, but I feel it's immaculately constructed and that any shmup junkie who hasn't yet ought to take it for a spin. The game is incredibly lightweight - having originally been designed with Dreamcast-era hardware in mind - so it'll even run on nearly anything!

I played the game with them voicing in Japanese because I just feel it’s weird if they speak English (I always prefer sub over dub ye)
The game takes about 40 hours to complete, for a total newb reading up on what to do as recommended by a guide and skipping all the side quests that are not mandatory to continue the main story. The 2D art and UI is top notch, plenty of detail and animation, excellent quality here. The dialogue can be really funny, sad or even disturbing at times. The maps are mostly like typical dungeons you see in typical RPG games, ranging from dark and spooky to colourful and happy dungeons. Saving in this game is punishing, (well for someone who is used to saving anytime I want) you can only save after you are out of a dungeon or close to the end of a dungeon. One thing that really annoyed me was the fact that some treasures in a dungeon require you to acquire items to break the boxes blocking your way. The feeling of a stupid treasure stuck there because you can see it but can’t get it is really infuriating. Luckily the guide helped me out and I continued the game without rage quitting.
The soundtrack in this game is just amazing. I never really bothered about most in game soundtracks at but all the ones in this game are really good. No words can say how good it is. Just listen to it yourself. Fits the theme of wherever you are pretty well. The sound design of most of the tracks are excellent. Nice sound staging, you can hear all the different instruments clearly and at different places. Also, neplunker I swear is rage inducing if you did not watch a guide and did the stupidest platforming for 30 mins dying for no reason at all due to bad coding.
I have not finished everything about the game, I just got the true ending (with a lot of raging as I needed to have an extra playthrough as I missed out something, good to see that there was more content in the true ending) and there is quite a bit more content compared to the other endings in the game (bad and good). Only fault I can see here is that the two other endings are lacking and they use the same exact outro video. I feel that they could have done more in making the other two endings more fleshed out and have more reason to go for that ending (especially the bad ending). Other than that, I genuinely enjoyed this game and I would recommend it to anyone new to this kind of genre or franchise.

Sooo... Paladins.
Let me get this out-of-the-way first; Paladins is fun. Matter of fact, it's very fun! The gameplay feels really nice when everything is working like you expect with enough unique characteristics to set it apart from other games in the genre, the maps are varied and fun if too few, the champion releases are really good for the most part with enough character in design and play style to get you invested as much as any other game like this, the art style is nice if a bit inoffensive and the community is generally good especially for a free to play game.
The business model was pretty bad but forgivable as a F2P game with all current and future champions being able to be bought in a relatively cheap and convenient pack but with most skins, some of which are really rather nice, being locked behind lootboxes. As I subscribe to the "lootboxes bought with real currency should be classified as gambling as they're made to prey on people like me with addictive personality disorders" this was almost a deal breaker but I found the game enjoyable enough to express my dislike while still having fun with the game.
Prior to the recent OB64 patch I would have recommended this game, with some minor-ish caveats, but sadly this patch has changed this.
Beyond all the stupid, inane and brain-dead (could probably chuck greedy in there as well) decisions they made in this patch honestly my biggest red flag for any new players is this; Hi-Rez don't seem to care. I honestly have no other explanation than they don't care about their core community that were in the VAST majority highly against this patch for so many well explained reasons that were given to them via feedback. They honestly don't seem to know or care what the players want with the CEO of Hi-Rez's letter to the community addressing the criticism firmly cementing this belief for me.
Not many people liked the earlier Essence system for buying cards but it was miles better than the massive changes they made to how cards, loadouts, levels and playlists all work now with all cards being unlocked from the start and having to level them from 1 to 10 by getting duplicates in fricking lootboxes. Not only that but they've somehow managed to make the VIP system feel even dirtier and split the fricking queues into new and changed modes so that the playerbase feels a lot smaller with longer load times.
This is getting a bit long and rambling now and there are other articles. reviews and videos of OB64 that explain the issues better, I highly recommend some of the Reddit posts from the last couple of weeks that broke down the patch into why it is so.....♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
In the end I'll just say this, if this game looks fun than sure, give it a download and try it, I'm not your boss. But I would strongly recommend not spending a cent on it, Hi-Rez don't care about you and seem to not care about the game all that much so why should you?

Deus Ex Human Revolution - Director’s Cut Review
Introduction:
Deus Ex HRDC is a first person shooter with RPG elements, set in the near future in a world where chaos and conspiracy are rife. The majority of the game is free roam and the choices you make during the game will effect the world around you. Based before the original Deus Ex you are placed in the role of Adam Jensen an ex-swat team member, who now finds him self in charge of security for one of the largest biotechnology firms in America.
Story:
The Deus games have always been driven on conspiracy theory’s, Human Revolution is no different. All through the game you will be questioning who to trust and who not to, friends may become enemiesand enemies friends. The story really does a great job of keeping you suspicious, your never sure if your a good guy or a bad one. Add to that some of the choices the game gives you with no clear moral option, you’ll find yourself constantly second guessing yourself.
But the story does feel rushed at times and some questions it rises never really feel answered, some moments feel unexplained. In fact if you turn the commentary on in extras they them selves will tell you they ran out of time to fully realize all they wanted to do. Its a shame as it really does show, But what’s there is good and achieves exactly what they were trying to.
Gameplay:
As of late I’ve been struggling to get in to FPS games as the market is so saturated, but Deus Ex HRDC does truly offer something different from the norm. The controls are a pretty standard fair with one or two odd key placements, but nothing that hampers the experience. But its the augmentations that really put this game apart, some being basic things like faster sprinting or improving hacking skills. But its the stealth augments and things like punching through walls that really make this fun, and stealth is a big element of Deus. Its possible if your careful and cleaver to get through almost every mission without firing a shot, but at times you will probably have to so lucky even your weapons are upgradeable too.
If I have one major criticism of the gameplay, its the cover system. When you take cover or use a take down move you move into 3rd person view, this is great for a visual effect but feels really jarring in practice. It just doesn’t flow right and left me feeling like they should have ether made the whole game in 3rd person or found a way to do it in 1st person. Even the option like Skyrim where you can use ether view I would have welcomed over the way its executed here, I also feel that FPS vets will probably not use the cover system anyway.
Presentation:
The graphics are great for a 2 year old game and really do give that futuristic atmosphere. Some maps do feel like your walking down the same corridor fifteen times as there all so similar, but this is to be expected. Thankfully most levels are in more open settings with a wider verity of surroundings. There at times is a almost Blade Runner feel to the game, this is really emphasized by the neon lit menus and displays in the game. The character models are great too, with every character seeming unique and fresh.
Conclusion:
I really enjoyed Deus, more than I thought I would. If your looking for something a little deeper than the standard FPS then really look no farther. With a deep plot that to me seem heavily inspired by the works of Isaac Asimov and gameplay that’s a little different I found it a real breath of fresh air. There’s really not a lot here not to like and I would recommend it highly to anyone into FPS games.

Rabi-Ribi is a game I think no one expected. I bought this game almost out of a whim and also thanks to LewdGamers review on the title. Rabi-Ribi is a fun mix of "Metroidvania" ( i like to call it Bunny-vania) with a bit of intense bullet-hell action. You control main protagonist, Erina. A rabbit who gets transfromed into a bunny girl who's in search of her master while pushing her way through the strange, vast world that she's in. Along the way she fights off against the world's hostile creatures and thirsty bunny fangirl fanatics with a piko hammer and a fairy named Ribbon who travels with Erina.
Pros:
-Cute 2D Character sprites
-The non-linear world of Rabi-Rabi Island is surprisingly big and the areas are well varied
-Boss fights are fun will test your bullet-hell dodging skills
-Music fits well with much of the game
-16-20+ Hour playthough
-Plenty of replayability even after clearing the game: Boss Rush, Speedrun mode, trying to get 100% on areas and items, Boss fight rankings, difficulty modes
-LOTS of achievements and trading cards to collect for all of you game achievement and steam card hunters!
Cons:
-When pausing the game, FPS seems to drop between high 40s to low 50s on a toaster rig I played on.
-Not a clear indication of how the areas connect to each other
-Minor Spelling errors ( though might of been fixed with updates)
-A number of boss fights are repeated late in the game, though they do mix things up with buffs/debuffs
-Outside of Erina's strange transformation and Rabi Rabi Island, the overall story feels inconsistant at times
Overall: Thumbs up! It's almost criminal how Rabi-Ribi fell under the radar. Do not be fooled by this games bright, cute and even mildly suggestive appearance. There's penty to do and explore in Rabi Rabi Island with intense bullet-hell action that well justifies the game at its $18 full price. I easily reccoment this game who are looking for a different spin on their non-linear action-platformers mixed with some bullet hell action and like cute bunny girls welding a piko hammer.

The story for The Secret Order 2: Masked Intent delves deeply into a historical organization that's shroud with mystery and conspiracy. The player takes on the role of a female protagonist named Sarah, who receives an abrupt phone call one night from her father's close friend. This man warns her that a current member of the Secret Five Order, Nathan, plans to use an unholy relic to disintegrate its members. It's up to the player, as Sarah, to solve all the puzzles and end Nathan's mad plot!
Before my brief playthrough, I was only aware of the existence of hidden object games but have never dedicated any time to playing one. I'm happy to say that I made the right choice in choosing this title to start. The hour I've played so far has been wonderous! What makes me  enjoy this game heavily is the simplistic style in the environment, addictive mini-games, and puzzles -- which first appear simplified by nature, but later on proves more complicated even for the more adept player. Players will successfully accomplish a variety of puzzles to progress through the story, unlocking additional content to the game like conceptual artwork and soundtrack that are easily located in the EXTRA menu. Thankfully, the game is equipped with a difficult setting so that those who would rather enjoy the story with little to no frustration can do so on casual, while those who enjoy a good challenge will have that option readily available, as well.

When Artifex Mundi publishes something that isn't their own work, you're often disappointed by the quality. While these games are still good and high quality, it's not what Artifex Mundi can deliver. And sometimes, you find a real gem, that could have been developed by them. Dark Heritages for example is one of these gems. Now, The Secret Order 2 is joining that club.
The story is a good one, though you wish that you played the first game to understand more the story. I mean, Nathan Williams, the bad guy, seemed to be related to the previous game (though it could be a mistake from my part). But, knowing you can travel through time (even if it's not really like in Time Mysteries, where you're going to different eras), you can expect some nice backgrounds. And you have them!
It's the Collector's Edition that is on Steam, so, the bonus chapter is already added in the middle of the story, when you're diving into a terrible atmosphere, with spirits, swamps and other cursed castles.
What I really loved in this game is that it's not too hard but not to easy: puzzles are well-balanced, HO scenes are also easy for some items but harder for others because of a matter of perspective (you're not used to see binoculars behind a piece of wood, showing their profiles or another item being upside down for example).
And the music.... it's really fitting to the game. Really fitting.
Anyway, my only complaint is the HUD that I find too big but you're getting used to that anyway.
If anything, buy that game. You'll enjoy it.
Now, I'm waiting for eventually for the first game to show up on Steam :)

Blockland has a bit of a history. In 2005, it was a little work-in-progress building game on the Torque Game Engine. Being an alpha, it had (here comes a massive understatement) quite a few mods that generated a larger following. The full game released in 2007, and much more polished than anything seen before. Streams of updates from the game's sole creator (with some collaboration thrown in) in the past six years have created a unique game that nothing can hope to come close to.
So, what's the main point? Blockland is That Game Where You Build Stuff. It's all on you, and the community. Using LEGO-like blocks to create structures in online multiplayer may sound mundane on paper, but the online part is where it really shines. The amount of creativity Blockland players have is nothing short of amazing. User-created add-ons like weapons and vehicles are plentiful, allowing for different and fun gamemodes within buildings YOU create, and an "events" system gives way for even more creativity within builds.
An accessible sandbox game for such a price is almost a steal.

The vanilla game may not have a ton to offer, so it all comes down to what the community has to offer (which is a ton). The gameplay makes it a lot like Gmod, except with a more consistant style. Additionally, it's multiplayer architecture makes joining servers with custom content seamless. You'll literally never need to actually install an add-on to play on a server with custom content (with a few exceptions, servers using custom GUI's may want you to install their GUI mods in order to play. This is usually optional anyways.)
The gamemode system adds a lot more 'out of the box' fun things to do than the game used to have. But it's still a bit underwhelming and you'll probably only get about a few hours of fun out of it if you refuse to install any add-on gamemodes or other things. Other than a few gamemodes available that are designed to be played in single-player, multiplayer is really where everything is at. There are a number of servers that have been developed for literally years and have a very high quality experience. If you ever really enjoyed Gmod at all, you'll probably find that the most fun servers in Blockland are ones where someone has simply set out a blank slate and a bunch of really neat mods. Shenanigans ensue.
It's a game you'll just keep coming back to.

This game might sound cheesy for some people at first glance. "I mean gee, a game where you play with legos online? What is this, people never heard of how bad Roblox turned out to be?!" (Personally I like games where you build stuff very fun, that's why I bought Blockland years ago in the first place...)
Oh trust me, it's a lot more than that. This game is like a fusion between Garry's Mod and Legos, but FAR easier to play. You can do pretty much anything in a stylized block world - houses, cities, deathmatches, survival games, racing tracks - and a lot more with its intuitive building and eventing system. Eventing is a sort of very very easy "scripting" within Blockland that you can use to make certain blocks to do certain things from within pre-set lists of actions that you can do to the block for it to do something you want and a lot more. It might seem very overwhelming at first, but when you start playing with it you'll get used to the idea quickly.
Building, in my opinion, is a little bit trickier, as you have to move "ghost blocks" around with the numpad (or some other buttons if you're on a numpad-less laptop) and then press enter to deploy a block, and they cannot be floating, nor penetrating the ground or other blocks, unless they are to be built within a Zone Brick which allows you to make actually floating blocks inside of it, so you don't have to make invisible supports for every floating island you might want to do. Buiilding is also very well optimized as you can do a number of moves with the ghost bricks to get them where you want and how you want quickly and efficiently; there exists a macro system where you can "save" the moves you do to a block so you can replicate patterns like stairs and stuff like that without much of a hassle. However, building can be clunky as you have to take blocks from a list to put them in your block selection list - you can only carry up to 10 blocks at a time, I believe.
However don't let this limit your creativity, as you can do pretty superb buildings in this game as evidenced by the game's great community - there is lots of support for this game, the developers and its players won't hesitate to help you with any problems you might have with the product, and there are just a LOT of addons in this game that do not allow it to ever be boring, especially with the Return to Blockland addon which is basically a community hub for the game, complete with a chat room, news, and a ton of other addons that are mounted into RTB for easy access, deactivation and (un)installation. RTB can also be downloaded for your server so you can get new Administration features, get the addons of your server listed in the server browser, so the players don't have to download it directly from your server (given they're hosted in RTB), and a few more features.
WARNING: Read the update above first. RTB is no longer functional, but there are backups.
Making addons for this game is, from what I understand, not tremendously difficult, and as long as you have the talent and willpower to make that one brick you can't find but need, or to make that weapon of your dreams, have a Ferrari in your garage or just a simple addition like a new face for your Blockhead, or maybe a song you want your Music Brick to play, all in all there is no (?) limit to the addons you can make for the game. I wish I could write from experience, but unfortunately, apart from a song or two I didn't make any addons for this game.
What I WAS ABLE TO do however was host servers and oh boy, coming from a person who can't ever host servers because of his connection not ever letting people connect, this was a HUGE plus for me. Even the player with the most blocked-off router can host games for their friends and never be hindered by issues like tremendous lag or timeouts, in my experience I found the netcode of Blockland to be very good. At least... I think this is the netcode's doing.
The gameplay is very appealing and so are the graphics, as they are very beautiful and, unsurprisingly, very colourful, stylized to look like a cartoon, similar to the likes of TF2, except on legos. Yeah. Graphics for me are very hard to describe. The "maps" (or just... plains) are roughly customizable so they have bodies of water or different types of surfaces, which can spice up the game a bit - I've always liked to build in maps with lots of water.
Overall, the game is very enjoyable and on the right servers it can be a ludicrous amount of fun. It is really amazing how such a simple and cheap game like this can provide so many hours of entertainment, from messing around with a few people to doing giant, elaborate buildings, from having mindless fast-paced deathmatch to having class-based capture the flag matches on carefully structured builds and just so much more. Blockland is truly a game for the ages, despite a few flaws like clunky building and some instances of lag when there are too many bricks within a server or when they're being duplicated.

Fun fast paced game with 15 minute long PvP matches. You can customize your guns choosing from multiple chassis: Rifle, which is a hitscan chassis with decent damage. Launcher, which fires a rocket (Or actually up to 6 rockets) and deals AoE damage. Pulse, which fires a spikey ball as projectile that deals some more damage then Rifle. And there is the Beam, with high hitscan damage at it's perfect range, but with a damage dropoff for ranges that are too close or too far away. There are a lot of different builds you can use and weaponparts you can buy with blutonium, this is the in-game currency that can only be gotten through playing. The other in-game currency is spacebux, which can only be brought with real-life money. WIth spacebux you can buy outfits and additional loadouts/weaponslots.
Lets move over to the pros and cons.
+Extremely fast paced gameplay
+Lots of fun weapons to create and use
+Art in the game is great
+Free to play (And no pay to win)
+No grinding
+Almost no cheaters
+No abusable voicechat system (I think this is a great thing)
+No abusable kick system
+Community-organized tournaments
+Active developers, also active on forums on official site.
+Fun and original gamemodes to play (Capture the flag with a giant hammer you can smash♥♥♥♥♥♥with. Extraction where you can throw chunks of blutonium to cause explosions)
Now the cons.
-High skill cap, this can be extremely frustrating to new players.
-Currently a low player-base
-Extremely small competitive community
-Relatively small amount of viable weapons in competitive scene
-Only 1 dev working on balance, this makes certain aspects of the game quite unbalanced. (Rifles are currently OP as hell)
There are some dissapointing cons, but that doesn't mean you shouldn't try out this game. It's free to play anyways and since 1 match only takes about 15 minutes you can get a nice first impression of the game and different gamemodes within just an hour. Try it out if you haven't yet!

I have been a fan of this genre from Dungeon Keeper 2 back in the day, and I can say that I thouroughly enjoy this iteration.  After the opening hours of the game, here are my initial impressions, pros and cons:
Pros:
Excellent writing and storytelling.  A self-aware commentary both on this particular series, and on fantasy games as a whole.
Great atmosphere and sound design.  It is both obvious and enjoyable to look at the evil dungeons as opposed to the good overworld.
The research tracks have greatly improved the sense of progression, and invests the player more in improving their dungeon.
Overall an homage and improvement to the original Dungeon Keeper series, much more so than previous iterations.
Cons:
Still a lackluster strategy game given the limited tactical controls and options.  While the dungeon building is the main focus, the overworld strategy game is a bit light, but a welcome addition to the series.
Some frustration at the dungeon building stage in balancing creature needs.
As mentioned, these are initial impressions and may change after a full playthrough.  For now, I definately reccomend the game for people who enjoy being evil, and those who have fond memories of the original Dungeon Keeper 2, a true homage to what Dungeon Keeper 3 could have been.

TL;DR : This game is a Nep/10
And so the game that is considered to be the one of the best entry in the Neptunia series finally stopped being a PS4 Exclusive and comes to steam, while it comes with a hefty price and hardware to even run this game, the game offers great enjoyment to those fans of Neptunia and newcomers alike.
In the Story department, this game does not require you to play all the previous titles in order to fully enjoy this game, Megadimension Neptunia VII delivers its story fairly well and welcomes newcomers to the series with open arms as this game is well safe aware of itself and will actually point out what you missed in the previous installments. The classical humor and jokes from the cast are still here, and you'll see why there's alot of memes around this series as a whole.
Presentation wise, this game is gorgeous, the artists did a really good job in to presenting the world your traversing through, the world looks vast and each dimension has its own unique atmosphere which correlates to the story in some way may it be Dark, Vibrant and Colorful or Sorrowful, you'll see these themes present as you play.
As for the gameplay, Megadimension rehashed alot of its gameplay elements from the previous titles, the overworld has been changed to give the overworld substance in between fighting and progressing the plot. And speaking of combat it has been redone in a way that scraps old mechanics in favor of new ones, some may see this as repetitive throughout the game but this is to be expected in a JRPG.
Sound is one of the major things this game is being praised for as it should, like everything else the music is miles better than its predecessors and the sound effects is very crisp and satisfying, from the Opening Title Theme to the Ending Credits Theme, I assure there will points where you will just drop everything in order to listen to the music, though be forewarned with your volume settings because some parts of this game doesn't know when to be loud or not.
All in all, Megadimension Neptunia VII is delivered nicely and is very welcoming to newcomers of the series, everything here is done miles better than what its previous titles did, and for the hefty price and hardware required this game is all worth your time and money, assuming you like dorky protagonists and anime girls but just don't delve into spoiler terrority before picking this up to ensure you get the full experience this game has to offer.

I went into this with low expectations. I was expecting gameplay to be meh, with more visual novel than game.
What I got was potentially the best-balanced, most original metroidvania I have seen in YEARS. I am 100% serious.
This game has:
* The map design of Metroid
* The movement mechanics of Castlevania
* A rather original combat system - the mechanics are unique
* A badge equip system vaguely reminding me of Paper Mario
* Touhou bullet-hell bosses.
Not to say that it is without faults - you literally need to go powerup hunting to beat some later bosses (and I'm on normal, seriously.)
But that said, if you want another great metroidvania game like Cave Story, or the genre namers - play this, even if you just fast forward the story. It 's worth it for the gameplay alone. "Easy" recommended for people who don't play bullet hells, since I'm getting obliterated in Chapter 4 on normal.
Oh, and this game works fine in WINE, by the way.

Likely to be polarising in more ways than one, Ikaruga is a milestone shooter well worth a peak for anyone interested in arcade shooters.
While I wouldn't recommend it as an entry point into the genre, due to it's complexity of gameplay and teeth-gnashing difficulty, it is a game I think everyone should at least take a punt at if they like games. Games period. Not just arcade games or shooters.
This is a really unique, artistically powerful and surreal experience to look at and play, and ranks up there easily with your Zeldas, your Final Fantasies and your ICOs in terms of impactful Japanese videogame art.
It also represents, if not the first, one of the first fully functional, recognisable polarity switching bullet systems in shooters. Personally I feel that the system does render the game marmite-style, in that it adds an extra layer of stuff to think about in a genre where you've normally got 240 different 'things to think about' coming at you at breakneck speed and that'll straight up drive some people insane, but back at it's original release, this game pioneered that mechanic.
Fundamentally, I think this game has been surpassed historically now, certainly in terms of fun and playability. This is a game designed to be gradually learned, not picked up and played, and the developer Treasure are notorious for difficulty and awkward complexities within simple genres (beaten Alien Soldier or Gunstar Future Heroes? No? Me neither...), and Ikaruga is no different. To me, you can feel that this game is nearly 15 or so years old not in it's look which is still remarkably fresh and unique, but in the feel of the gameplay. Newer shooters are faster, more responsive and universally easier to actually play well.
Ikaruga will punish you mercilessly for getting things wrong. Pick the wrong polarity at any given moment and you will die instantly, respawning in the wrong colour straight into the same bullet curtain that just killed you. Press the swap polarity button a fraction of a second too late and you'll be torn to shreds during the agonisingly 'just. too. slow.' polarity swap animation.
It also won't let you record any kind of highscore, local or global, unless you play with only 3 lives and no continues. Download the demo and you'll see how utterly cruel a yardstick that is.
Fundamentally, if you're looking for any kind of easy ride, or a soft entry point into the genre, buy something else.
This is a game that entices you in with stunning artwork, amazing sound and a genuinely atmospheric world, and then tackles you to the floor and beats the living daylights out of you. It demands respect, and it is sometimes the complete polar opposite of fun to play because of it's insanely steep learning curve.
Because of that, I really recommend firmly downloading the demo and playing it over and over until you're sure you enjoy the game. At it's core, this is a mean, vicious, downright insane game that will troll you at every turn, BUT, it is, much like all the best difficult games, very rewarding when you do start to get the hang of it.
And dear god, it's gorgeous. Absolutely stunning.

Doom is one of the best FPS games I've ever played, and I have played many.
Pros:
+ The game has gorgeous visuals, with great 'optimization', running very smoothly for how good it looks.
+ The soundscape is fantastic, with a great soundtrack, and tense atmosphere.
+ The gameplay is fast paced, exciting, gory, sometimes scary, and very intense, especially at higher difficulty levels.
+ The single player has a good amount of replay value with hidden secrets, exploration, and collectibles.
+ The DLC was recently made free for owners of just the base game.
Cons:
- Sometimes the game can be frustrating with gaps between checkpoints, and enemy spawns which sometimes result in unavoidable deaths.
- There are a few bugs here and there, however most have been ironed out in recent patches.
- Multiplayer is hit and miss, it can be hard to find a game sometimes, there are server lag issues, and often unbalanced teams, ultimately MP is fun and not serious.
- Due to the ludicrous MP achievements it takes a long time to 100% the game.

I grew up playing the original alpha of this game, it was called Blockland v00002, lagged like a mofo and it was barely playable on my Pentium 4 PC. But, most importantly, it was fun.
Then a bunch of years later, this game came out - and it is just absolutely amazing. Think of it as a sort of lego-builder's Garry's Mod. Sure, you've got your great building tools to make awesome♥♥♥♥♥♥with your friends in the default sandbox mode, within the limitations (it's still lego, so you can't have any floating bricks, for example), but apart from that, anyone can create new weapons, vehicles, and entirely new gamemodes with the game's scripting language (the uh, not terribly excellent TorqueScript).
And the builds you make can be enhanced with event bricks, which are basically interactive bricks that'll react to say, a player walking on it, in ways that you define in the game with a simple system. Some dude made a playable pong using that, which is batshit crazy. And awesome.
All in all, I can't find a good way to end this, because I'm not a writer, but I really, truly love this game, and I wish more people would play it with me.

If you've already converted yourself to an Xbox 360 controller you will probably hate this controller.  What was easy before now becomes harder.  Look up a guide asking for tips and it will tell you to wash the controller with sudsy warm soap water and wash your thumbs too.  Maybe that article was a joke (I don't care to take more time and figure it out) but the controller is too ambitious.
If you are a keyboard and mouse player who doesn't like a conventional controller then this might be a good fit (I don't know, I'm not that guy, I like the xbox 360 controller).
My Experience:
- Packaging - looks nice at first, controller has all kinds of white dust (from the packaging), blow it off with a can of air. I know it's because of the white packaging inside - but having to air dust something new makes me think that these things are made in a dusty mill somewhere.  I can't remember seeing this in any gadget I've ever received.
- Use - works like a controller.  Be prepared for almost every game you play to ask you to make a determination right away about how you want to use the controller with the game.  Going back to the game won't reveal any way of changing these settings. I'm praying that my ceasing to use this controller fixes this - worried I'll pronbably need to make a support call to clear my settings.
- No easy way to just use an xbox 360 controller instead.  Every game will act as if you are trying to use it with the Steam controller.
- Batteries are installed in a weird very stiff install process.  My unit came with Duracell Alkaline batteries - I ignored that and used rechargables.  No idea if the rechargable batteries were reacharged or not, I didn't give this controller more than 2 hours of time but I had to remove the batteries in order to return and I had to use a knife to dig them out (was the way that the xbox 360 did it that much of a hinderence? what a weird choice).
A controller that promises to make everything better should not take training to use, it shouldn't arrive dusty, it should have more documentation, it should be rechargable (it might be, never bothered to care), it shouldn't be mostly weird.
If you are a keyboard player and want to move over (not up- it's a preference) to a gamepad, maybe this is the thing for you.  The frustration you will feel is simlar (maybe worse) than the frustration you will feel moving from WASD controls to a standard controller.

This is my first review on the Neptunia series as the past games I felt were covered enough by the reviews, however this game I was just blown away with and I wanted to voice my input on it.
The game continues from where Re;Birth 3 left off and is followed by 3 stories in one game, all 3 stories are within their own dimensions. Zero Dimension, Hyperdimension and Heart Dimension. Each story/dimension had it's own feel which made it feel like 3 different games, however keeping true to the Neptunia series. Zero Dimension was in my opinion one of the better stories solely off of how it was told. It was a lot more serious, has a more darker story behind it and you actually worry about the survival of the characters during this story, that is how well it was written. Hyperdimension wasn't as serious as Zero Dimension, Hyperdimension kept more of the aspect of keeping the randomness, the jokes, the 4th wall breaking that is a staple of the Neptunia series. Heart Dimension was a pretty good closer as well. The story felt mixed with Zero Dimension and Hyperdimension but there was a lot more twists in Heart Dimension. I always thought Re;Birth 2 had the more serious story but Megadimension took that over easily. I would go as far to say that this has so far been the best story out of the series and I truthfully enjoyed Re;Birth's 3 story more than any of the previous games as I felt it covered a lot more, but once against Megadimension toppled that.
Upon starting the game, you will notice quite an upgrade in graphics. Movies look a lot more smoother and stable, the menu and UI look a lot more sleeker, the artwork and text box in the visual novel parts of the game look a lot more crisper and higher quality and the actual gameplay looks and feels a lot better. Animation looping is also a lot more smoother than previous games. The CG in this game also got quite an increase in quality and detail, some of which look stunning.
This soundtrack was phenomenal. OST in games is always something that is a huge importance to me and the Neptunia series has always had a good amount OST that I enjoyed listening to while playing the game. Megadimension has a new OST while keeping previous music from other games. The new OST I feel they went above and really did a fantastic job on it. Every dimension has their own version of music, be that the over-world, in the dungeon(s) or enemy battles and they did a great job of getting those soundtracks to match the feel of that dimension.
Some new things have been added to gameplay.
- The Guard Break from previous games is now changed to Part Break in which certain areas of an enemy are guarded that need to be broken to deal more damage, such as their head, behind them, their sides. There is no longer a Break attack, it is just a Standard attack. Attacking an enemy with Parts on it will be be broken overtime regardless of the moves used against them.
- The over-world has changed completely. You no longer freely pick where you want to go, instead it's mapped out and you travel to the places (best compared to like Super Mario 3 over-world.) Upon traveling to a place in the over-world you have a chance to encounter a battle. This is completely random as you can encounter enemies every 2 steps or you can run the whole map and not fight a single enemy. This can become repetitive as the enemies become weak as you level up, their EXP and credit drop stops being worth it and you may just want to get to somewhere quicker. After you beat the game and start NG+, you get an item that lets you disable or enable random encounters in the over-world.
- Scouts make a return again but this time a little different, however a lot better in my opinion. The new scouting system works similar to the Fury system in Fairy Fencer F. You select a scout or scouts and send them to a dungeon or split them up into multiple dungeons. Each scout has a dungeon effect be that a positive or negative effect. Such as +10% credits and -5% EXP. The scouts run on a timer to complete a dungeon and when they return they will bring you items from the enemies there, credits, a chance at a new dungeon for you the explore, a chance for a new scout or scouts to join, a hidden treasure hint and will find 2 new enemies for you to battle, which are bosses. The hidden treasure hint is how to get a hidden treasure for that dungeon only. There are certain steps you have to do in order to complete that one hit such as win 5 battles without healing, win against 5 dogoos in a row, ect. One thing you will find from a good portion of hidden treasures is an item called Energy Mate, which is used to level up your scouts. The higher level your scouts are, the more items and credits they will find, as well as the chances for scouts to join.
- Combo Trait is a new feature added to your attacks. Before each attack, you may notice that one or more attacks may be glowing, that is how you start the combo train. When using this, all attacks for that combo will always hit and will always be critical hits.
- The EX Finish is no longer here in the form of a combo like in previous games. Instead there is now Coupling Skills, which when you get the required EXE, in your skill menu you can use the Coupling Skill. There is also now Formation Skills which work by having certain party members in the battle in a certain formation to use a skill. They all have to be in normal or HDD forms for them to work.
Example: Neptune and Nepgear in a battle, both must be in HDD or in their normal forms. One cannot be HDD and normal at the same time for it to work. You can have a 4 person formation attack, however the same applies they must all be in HDD or normal form and you must make the correct form (on the skill page you may have to be in a triangle formation for a 3 person attack, a square for 4 person attack or "sandwich" an enemy for a 2 person attack
- When in the skill menu during a battle, I have noticed that when cycling through the skills quickly, I get some slight frame drops (my hardware is not the issue.)
- Random encounters. As I mentioned above with the over-world, random encounters can become repetitive. I have the item that stops that, however until then, the endgame was getting a little tedious with all the random encounters.
Story: Very well written, serious moments while keeping true to the Neptune series of having funny and random moments.
Graphics: Graphics look a lot cleaner and smoother than the previous games. Looping animation is also a lot smoother than previous games.
Soundtrack: Honestly, one of the better OSTs I've heard in a while, they really stepped it up big.
Gameplay: A lot of new stuff added which adds to the experience of the game.
Neptune:

If you have been a fan of the Neptunia series or you like JRPG's in general, definitely give this game a go. The price might push some away, but it's honestly worth with the amount they included into this game. The story is honestly worth getting into and like I stated above, there's a lot of humour, seriousness and plot twists. They really outdid themselves with this story and I really enjoyed this story and game in general. If you haven't played Re;Birth2 or Re;Birth 3, there will be multiple references you won't get, however that will not make it so you can't play the game at all, you can jump into this game as your first Neptunia game and still play the game no problem, learn slightly about previous games and that always gives you the headroom for going back to play the previous ones. If you get the DLC and don't want to make the game too easy, I would use it after you beat the game once. A lot of the weapons and armour make the game way too easy.
I would highly recommend as a purchase!

It's a great contoller! Really is. It's takes a couple of hours to really get used to it, but with most new tech that's usually the case. Aside from a normal configuration that you are most likely aquanted with in other controllers this one has two touchpads for joysticks that work wonderfully. They really do give you some great precision and allow you to jump into PC games that you might no otherwise be able to on a regular controller. There are also two grip buttons on that back in case you need to more keys assigned to the controller or would appreciate the shortcut to on, there are also some motion controlls you can play with and customiziton option that get pretty wild once you get in them, finding the right configuration for yourself can be fun on it own. The only issue I have with the contoller and why I might not reccommend it to someone is the joystick. There is a built in joystick. It might seem like a great option, but when you add up the two touchpads what you have are three joysticks.
This controller could have done with a traditional D-Pad. The right touchpad can emulate a D-Pad, but is a poor substitute for one. Playing 2D games feels a but upsetting and a joystick just doesn't do it justice. Fighting games also seem to lose uumph because of it to. I bought two controllers to be able to use with friends and they all felt controller fatigue and to be honest I did as well, this coming from an experience from playing games like Guilty Gear and to a poaint Evoland. I'd like to say that with a little more time with the controller maybe this will be a problem that would fix itself, but that doesn't seem to be the case. With traditional controllers there was a reason that some things were just better to do on the D-Pad than on a joystick and that shows here. The draw of paladins over its competitors, was the ability to customize your champion by using the 12 point card system they had in place. Each skill has 4 different cards you could use to buff the ability. Those cards would then have 4 points total that you could place a point into to buff it even further, which is how you customized your champion to fit your playstyle. It was fun being able to experiment and tinker with these cards. You were able to create a playstyle that assisted in very specific strategies you had in mind to beat your opponents. It wasn't the most in-depth system, but it didn't have to be to accomplish very speciifc goals..which were to give the player a sense of control on how they wanted to play the champion.
With the new patch OB64, they changed how this works. You no longer can adjust the numbers for each specific card you get to buff your skill. If you already owned the card, it gets set to level 4 (out of 10). The only way you can level up your card is opening chests and getting duplicates of that card. When you have enough duplicates it will level up your skill. There is no longer a point limit, so you can have all 5 equippable slots filled with level 10 cards and have an advantage over someone who does not have level 10 cards.
Now, Hi-rez's solution to this was making this a different game mode than ranked/casual play. It's apart of the "arcade" now. That would be perfectly fine if the system still didn't leak over to the other game modes. What I mean in they set all your cards to default at level 4...and that's it. You don't get to tinker with the numbers anymore and cater it to your playstyle. Hi-Rez just gave us cards with set power that we can't change, which now fundamentally changes how we play our favorite champions. They took a large part of customization within the game for the reason (from which I assume) of it being easier to balance.
To sum the changes up..what they essentially accomplished was created a mode for whales and grinders, took away large parts of customization from everyone and overall made the game more bland. I don't see any major positive changes from this patch. In the end it is still paladins, it will still be possible to have fun with this title. But when I'm essentially handed the game back after a patch, and all it has to offer is less than what it was, then for me I'll just put it on the shelf and wait. I will still hold onto hope that a better system in time will replace this one. Perhaps maybe even appropriate adjustments will be made to give me that personal feeling of customization with my champion I had, before this patch.
If you are on the edge of checking this game out, I would wait a few weeks to see what they decide to do.

That said, the game is full of content and sports even a co-op mode - which is lovely to have. Between a good (if predictable) campaign, solid skirmish and multiplayer it has a lot to offer.
So if you dont want to spend all your time fighting, and enjoy the fun of building a fancy trap filled death dungeon this might be one to pick up.

Featuring a campaign that has a lot of the same hit-or-miss (mostly miss) humor as before, the game thankfully introduces random skirmish maps that can be used offline or online for vastly increased replay value. In addition, the interface is improved with an actual mouse pointer and better unit selection. The gameplay structure is the same as before: find the gold nuggets, place rooms to house units and produce resources, hire new units, and place defenses. However, new to the game is a research tree, which uses evil points accumulated by capturing locations on the Overworld map, forcing you to venture out of the dungeon in order to unlock the more advanced dungeon options required to win each scenario. While the flow of each game is the same, the random maps help immensely in creating a slightly different feel each time. The newest entry in the Dungeons series fixes the major problems from the last iteration by adding in random maps and improving the interface, finally making it a compelling management game.

Tough as nails and beautiful to behold.
Ikaruga and its spiritual predecessor Radiant Silvergun (which I hope to one day see on steam) are the pinnacle of the shoot em up genre, made by the masters at Treasure. Flawless controls, top notch unique designs and oozing character from every bullet-ridden pore. If more shmups were this good the genre would be a lot more than an almost forgotten relic from arcade days past and a playground for uncreative indie developers (sorry guys, everybody and their moms can make a generic shmup).
Ikaruga owes a lot to its grandfather "Space Invaders", like any other vertical-scrolling shooter but cleverly subverts the basic concept by giving you a colour-switching mechanic: red/black bullets only hurt you when you are white/blue and vice versa. However if you think this will make the game easy you are mistaken. The screen is filled with artful patterns of red and blue that will give you an intense challenge and plenty of replay value, because you will die and die a lot. There are no power-ups, no shields, just a super shot that fills up by collecting bullets which quickly becomes necessary to survive at all. Get hit once and you are dead of course. The gameplay offers more layers of complexity and challenge when you want to go for the big points. Shooting 3 enemies of one colour in a row will chain your points together. Skillful players can continue this chain from beginning to end of each level, although at first it might seem impossible to newcomers.
The game can be a bit bare bones if you are not a shoot em up fan with only 5 levels in total, but these blow pretty much the whole competition out of the water. The steam port also offers crisp HD graphics, a selection of unlockable artworks and an incredibly well-made leaderboard section. You can quickly download every playthrough from other players and thus learn how to survive this one of a kind bullet hell extravaganza.
Developer support is also great. I bought Ikaruga when it was first released and at first it wasn't possible to play offline or on older Windows XP systems (which were at the end of their lifespan but still supported) as promised on the store page, both were patched in a matter of days by the developers who genuinely want to give players a good experience.
All in all one of my best purchases on steam. Ikaruga was worth the 9000Yen I paid back in the day on dreamcast, at this price it is a steal.

For those wondering about it, this is a prequel to Deus Ex. The storyline, in order, is Human Revolution, The Fall, Deus Ex, then Invisible War. While I have yet to play completely through all of them, I can honestly say it is a rather amazing series (The Fall leaves a bit to be desired, but is decent enough).
As it has been stated, but must be reiterated, you have to be able to think about things outside your normal comfort zone sometimes with this game. It will make you question what is morally right and wrong. In my opinion though, that is what makes a good story. Anything that can make you think outside your normal comfort zone and make you question everything you have ever known to be true.
The gameplay for this, is actually rather difficult. Yes, guards and people will walk specific paths or stand still in one area, making it easy enough to pass, but if you are noticed, they WILL search for you. Stealth is definitely a fun, yet occasionally frustrating way to play. Especially later on, when tough choices have to be made. Going lethal can also be fun enough if you're into that sort of run and gun action. Enemies will make you think about how best to tackle them. This isn't CoD where you can soak a thousand shots before dying. If you get focused by several enemies and absorb their fire, you WILL die.
The RPG elements of this game are a little frustrating. There aren't many skill points, especially early on, and leveling takes a while. You'll need skills in hacking and such to continue on a lot of the time.
That's one of the few things I feel really needed to be improved. I will say this though, exploration is your friend. There are so many alternate ways to get passed or defeat almost anything.

bullethell metroidvania.  i like it a lot.
the bosses are a lot of fun to fight, become rather challenging late game (and some even early game), and the combat is frantic with you trying to squeeze as much damage in between attacks while dodging bullets.  they're varied and rarely seem unfair, aside from a single midgame boss i didn't feel that any of the attack patterns were too outlandish to feasibly dodge.  you also get temporary invuln that charges up which you can spend with the press of a button.  it also stuns enemies which means you can get in extra damage before the game gives them super armor to go to their next attack.
the metroidvania aspect of it is just okay.  it provides a nice change of pace between the hectic bosses but doesn't feel especially well done.  it isn't really a challenge to get from point A to B until you get to the very last area of the game.
but the bosses are so fun that it really doesn't matter to me.  i got way more enjoyment out of this game than i was expecting from watching trailers and earlygame streams, and for 15 bucks it's probably my favorite single player game i've played in the last few years.  i've still got a lot more to go if i want, too.
